note: Data for the US AI Data Center Tracker at energyriskengineering.com/data-center-tracker. Edit this file to update the live page.

projects.name: Stargate Abilene
projects.status_note: All eight buildings are topped out. Buildings 1-2 have run since late 2025, about six had been handed to OpenAI by late September 2026, and the last four are expected fully running around November 2026.
projects.power_source: 1.2 GW ERCOT interconnection with new 1 GW substation, onsite gas-turbine plant, behind-the-meter solar and batteries
projects.cooling: Closed-loop direct-to-chip liquid with air-cooled free-cooling chillers (no evaporation)
projects.water_source: Not disclosed (closed loop, zero evaporative use claimed)
projects.cost_note: $15B Crusoe/Blue Owl JV for the 1.2 GW campus. Epoch AI puts it near $31.9B including IT hardware. 1.2 GW is facility power; online MW is Epoch's IT estimate.
projects.next_milestone: Buildings 5-8 fully operational (campus complete)
projects.key_risks: A planned expansion past 1.2 GW was dropped amid financing problems and shifting OpenAI demand; Microsoft took the adjacent 900 MW. Full output depends on the onsite gas plant and new substation.

projects.name: Stargate Frontier (Shackelford)
projects.status_note: Shells for buildings 1-5 are complete and roofed, cooling and generators are going into buildings 1-3, and foundations have started on 6-7. Vantage targets first delivery in late 2026; Epoch's filing-based estimate is mid-2027.
projects.power_source: Off-grid behind-the-meter gas microgrid by VoltaGrid (Jenbacher reciprocating engines, about 700 MW first phase)
projects.utility: None (off-grid VoltaGrid microgrid in ERCOT region)
projects.cooling: Closed-loop chilled water with combined air and liquid-to-liquid cooling for 250 kW+ racks
projects.water_source: Not disclosed (Vantage claims near-zero WUE)
projects.cost_note: $25B+ Vantage campus figure. TDLR filings register $10.64B of construction; Epoch projects about $53B with IT hardware. 1,400 MW is critical IT load.
projects.next_milestone: First data center building delivered
projects.key_risks: Depends entirely on a major-source gas plant, its TCEQ air permit and gas supply; the Sept 2026 Texas pause on new TCEQ data-center permits adds uncertainty. SoftBank's pending acquisition of Vantage parent DigitalBridge.

projects.name: Stargate Milam (Freebird)
projects.status_note: The first-phase building (548,950 sq ft, four data halls) topped out in March 2026 and state filings show completion around October 2026. No capacity confirmed online yet.
projects.power_source: SB Energy-funded new generation and storage (type not disclosed) plus ERCOT grid
projects.cooling: Not disclosed
projects.water_source: Not disclosed (designed to minimize water use)
projects.cost_note: $3B is SB Energy's earlier campus plan; the phase-1 TDLR filing is about $470M. Epoch projects about $32.5B with IT. 1.2 GW is OpenAI's lease figure.
projects.next_milestone: Phase-1 building completion per TDLR filing
projects.key_risks: Power supply plan not public; execution depends on SoftBank/SB Energy financing and a new fast-build modular approach.

projects.name: Stargate Lordstown
projects.status_note: The former GM/Foxconn plant is being refit mainly as a factory for modular data-center equipment plus a smaller data-center component. Nothing operating yet; one tracker lists the data-center use as withdrawn.
projects.power_source: Grid via existing plant substation
projects.cooling: Not disclosed
projects.water_source: Not disclosed
projects.cost_note: Up to $3B for SoftBank's plant conversion, mostly manufacturing. 214 MW is Epoch's IT estimate.
projects.next_milestone: First data-center capacity operational (Epoch projection)
projects.key_risks: Unclear how much of the site will be a data center versus a factory. Village data-center permit moratorium extended in July 2026; local opposition over noise, heat and water.

projects.name: Project Jupiter (Doña Ana)
projects.developer: STACK Infrastructure (Blue Owl) and BorderPlex Digital Assets
projects.status_note: Data-center buildings were about 26% complete in September 2026. The fuel-cell microgrid awaits its state air permit and its gas pipeline has slipped to February 2027; Oracle sent a force-majeure notice while saying the schedule holds.
projects.power_source: Private onsite gas microgrid of about 2.46 GW of Bloom solid-oxide fuel cells, fed by the new Transwestern pipeline; up to 2 GW of off-site renewables sought
projects.cooling: Closed-loop non-evaporative
projects.water_source: Non-potable industrial well water (purchased farm water rights)
projects.cost_note: $165B is the developers' full-buildout estimate and county IRB authorization. 2.45 GW is campus design draw.
projects.next_milestone: NMED decision on microgrid air permit
projects.key_risks: Contested microgrid air permit, State Land Office pipeline right-of-way denial and pending FERC authorization, litigation over county bonds and incentives, and strong local opposition.

projects.name: Stargate Michigan (The Barn)
projects.status_note: All three 550,000 sq ft buildings are under construction; the first was described as nearly finished in June 2026. Completion targeted late 2027, operations early 2028.
projects.power_source: DTE grid from existing resources plus project-funded battery storage
projects.cooling: Closed-loop air-cooled system; water use said to be similar to an office building
projects.water_source: Not disclosed
projects.cost_note: $16B development and construction (up from about $7B). Totals near $43-56B are reported including Oracle's equipment fit-out. 1.4 GW is DTE's contracted supply.
projects.next_milestone: First building energized and delivered to Oracle
projects.key_risks: AG and environmental groups are appealing the MPSC's approval of the DTE contracts; local opposition after a consent judgment overrode the township's rezoning denial; possible repeal of Michigan's data-center tax break.

projects.name: Stargate Lighthouse (Port Washington)
projects.status_note: Four roughly 550,000 sq ft buildings are rising with about 3,000 workers on site, but the campus cannot run until a new ATC transmission line is approved; the PSC sent that application back in August 2026.
projects.power_source: We Energies grid via a dedicated rate: new solar, wind and battery projects plus a proposed 10-20% share of Point Beach nuclear output; diesel emergency generators
projects.cooling: Closed-loop liquid cooling
projects.water_source: Municipal (new city water main)
projects.cost_note: $15B+ Vantage campus figure, excluding the $1.3-2B+ ATC transmission project. Other sources cite a 1.3 GW grid request.
projects.next_milestone: PSC review of refiled ATC transmission application; ruling on Point Beach nuclear deal
projects.key_risks: Transmission delay: an analyst projects meaningful load no earlier than mid-to-late 2028. Lawsuit against DNR over environmental review; resident opposition over transmission costs and noise.

projects.name: Meta Hyperion
projects.status_note: Roofs are on the first two halls and the cooling plant is being installed, but nothing is energized yet. In July 2026 Meta raised the target to 5 GW and the investment to more than $50B.
projects.power_source: Entergy Louisiana grid plus 3 approved new combined-cycle gas plants (7 more requested), solar, batteries and new 500 kV transmission
projects.cooling: Air-cooled chillers (about 816 planned, per satellite imagery); liquid loop design not disclosed
projects.water_source: Not disclosed (Meta pledges 100% local watershed replenishment)
projects.cost_note: Meta's July 2026 figure of more than $50B (was $10B at groundbreaking, about $27B in the Blue Owl JV). 5,000 MW is Meta's stated compute target; Epoch counts about 1,632 MW of IT by 2028.
projects.next_milestone: First new Entergy gas units in service; PSC ruling on 7 more gas plants
projects.key_risks: Relies on regulators approving 7 more Entergy gas plants; a PSC commissioner warns of stranded costs. Scrutiny of off-balance-sheet bond financing and fast-track approvals.

projects.name: Meta Prometheus
projects.status_note: Most buildings and tent halls are running AI clusters; expansion continues while Williams finishes two behind-the-meter gas plants for the remaining halls.
projects.power_source: AEP Ohio grid (250 MW interim) plus Williams Socrates South/North behind-the-meter gas plants (400 MW) with batteries; a third plant (about 250 MW) projected for 2028
projects.utility: AEP Ohio / PJM; Williams onsite gas
projects.cooling: Direct-to-chip liquid in AI halls; air-assisted liquid racks in older halls
projects.water_source: Municipal (New Albany)
projects.cost_note: Epoch AI's projected capex for full build. Meta has disclosed only about $1.5B invested since 2017. MW figures are Epoch IT estimates; Meta's target is 1 GW by end of 2026.
projects.next_milestone: Socrates South and North gas plants fully in service
projects.key_risks: Growth depends on on-time Williams gas plants; the AEP grid feed is temporary with an 85% minimum-demand charge; onsite gas emissions draw scrutiny.

projects.name: Meta El Paso
projects.status_note: Vertical construction is under way on the 1 GW campus; a majority stake went to BlackRock in July 2026. Texas judges proposed approving the dedicated 366 MW gas plant only if ratepayers bear none of its cost.
projects.power_source: El Paso Electric grid (about 220 MW) plus a proposed 366 MW plant of modular gas generators next to the campus
projects.cooling: Closed-loop water cooling (per Meta)
projects.water_source: Not disclosed
projects.cost_note: Total development cost in the July 2026 BlackRock JV announcement (was $1.5B, then $10B+). The gas plant is a separate ~$0.5B.
projects.next_milestone: Texas PUC vote on the McCloud gas plant certificate
projects.key_risks: PUCT could deny or restrict the gas plant; the City of El Paso and over 1,000 residents oppose it. Texas's Sept 2026 pause on TCEQ data-center permits adds uncertainty.

projects.name: Meta Lebanon (LEAP District)
projects.status_note: Ground broken in February 2026 on a 1,500-acre, 13-building campus; first phase aimed at late 2027 or early 2028.
projects.power_source: Grid supply from Boone REMC / Wabash Valley Power Alliance, matched with 409 MW of new Indiana renewables
projects.cooling: Closed-loop liquid cooling that recirculates water (per Meta)
projects.water_source: Municipal (Lebanon / LEAP supply from Citizens Energy Group)
projects.cost_note: Meta's stated figure of more than $10B across up to six phases.
projects.next_milestone: First phase online
projects.key_risks: Controversy over moving regional water to the LEAP District, rate-impact concerns, and dependence on new transmission.

projects.name: xAI Colossus 1
projects.status_note: The converted Electrolux plant is fully running; since May 2026 Anthropic has leased all of its compute while xAI training moved to Colossus 2.
projects.power_source: MLGW/TVA grid (about 300 MW) plus permitted onsite gas turbines, Megapack batteries and adjacent solar
projects.cooling: Evaporative cooling towers (33 units), replacing air-cooled chillers by Feb 2026
projects.water_source: Municipal (MLGW, Memphis aquifer); planned $80M wastewater recycling plant stalled
projects.cost_note: Epoch AI's estimated capex. MW is Epoch's IT estimate.
projects.next_milestone: Construction restarts on the wastewater recycling plant
projects.key_risks: Environmental-justice opposition and air-permit disputes over the gas turbines; aquifer drawdown concerns while the recycling plant is delayed; Memphis council moratorium vote set for Oct 20.

projects.name: xAI Colossus 2
projects.status_note: Two large clusters on Tulane Road run close to 1 GW; a third building is under construction. Power comes from temporary gas turbines in Southaven, MS, to be replaced by a permitted 1.2 GW permanent plant.
projects.power_source: Mostly self-generated gas: temporary turbines in Southaven, MS, to be replaced by a 41-turbine 1.2 GW plant; Megapacks and some MLGW supply
projects.cooling: Air-cooled (dry) chillers and air-cooled condenser arrays
projects.water_source: Not disclosed
projects.cost_note: Epoch AI's projected capex. MW are Epoch IT estimates; Musk has claimed 2 GW eventually.
projects.next_milestone: Permanent Southaven gas plant in service; temporary turbines retired by July 2027
projects.key_risks: NAACP Clean Air Act suit, a residents' class action and an appeal of the MDEQ permit target the Southaven turbines; continuing local opposition to air pollution.

projects.name: Microsoft Fairwater (Wisconsin)
projects.status_note: Building 1 was completed and fully running by June 2026 after an April startup. Building 2 next door is under construction for 2028, and grading for a larger expansion has begun.
projects.power_source: We Energies grid; matched with carbon-free supply including 250 MW of solar; backup generators
projects.cooling: Closed-loop liquid for over 90% of the facility, outside air for the rest; air-cooled heat rejection
projects.water_source: Racine Water Utility (Lake Michigan); about 2.8M gal/yr for Phase 1
projects.cost_note: $3.3B for building 1 plus $4B for building 2 (Microsoft). Epoch estimates about $27.9B including chips. MW are Epoch IT estimates.
projects.next_milestone: Building 2 energized (Epoch projection)
projects.key_risks: Neighbor complaints about cooling-fan noise; ratepayer pushback on We Energies rate increases for about 2.6 GW of new Microsoft load.

projects.name: Microsoft Fairwater Atlanta (QTS Fayetteville)
projects.status_note: Fairwater 2 began running in October 2025 and buildings 3-4 were operating by mid-June 2026. QTS has two more shells under way on the 615-acre campus, tenant unconfirmed.
projects.power_source: Utility grid only, no onsite generation or UPS for the GPU fleet; onsite storage smooths power swings
projects.cooling: Closed-loop direct-to-chip liquid with a very large air-cooled chiller plant (about 672 units)
projects.water_source: Fayette County municipal (closed loop; small initial fill)
projects.cost_note: Epoch AI estimate including chips for buildings 1-4. Microsoft has not disclosed a cost. MW is Epoch's IT estimate.
projects.next_milestone: Fit-out of two more QTS building shells
projects.key_risks: No backup generation for the GPU halls means full utility dependence; a water-billing dispute over unmetered lines at the QTS campus; regional opposition to data-center water use.

projects.name: Microsoft Pecos
projects.status_note: Announced June 2026 with a 20-year supply deal from a co-located Chevron gas plant; capacity added over 5-7 years and no construction start published.
projects.power_source: Co-located behind-the-meter gas plant up to 2.67 GW (GE Vernova and Solar Turbines), later grid tie
projects.utility: None at launch; future ERCOT interconnection
projects.cooling: Closed-loop; initial fill only
projects.water_source: Non-potable and brackish groundwater; possible produced-water reuse
projects.cost_note: Microsoft gives only a multibillion-dollar figure.
projects.next_milestone: First power from Chevron's gas plant
projects.key_risks: Depends on Chevron building a large gas plant on schedule (turbines, air permits) amid Texas's permit pause; no grid backup at launch.

projects.name: AWS Project Rainier (New Carlisle)
projects.status_note: Phases 1-2 (18 buildings) largely run Trainium chips for Anthropic; buildings 17-18 expected around October 2026. A 14-building expansion is in site prep awaiting air and wetlands permits.
projects.power_source: I&M grid (nuclear, coal, wind) matched by about 635 MW of Amazon Indiana wind/solar; diesel backup only
projects.cooling: Mostly outside air with water-assisted cooling on hot hours; expansion adds direct-to-chip liquid
projects.water_source: New Carlisle municipal wells (shallow aquifer)
projects.cost_note: $11B AWS announced investment. Epoch estimates $72.9B at full build including chips. 2,200 MW is AWS grid draw; online MW is Epoch's IT estimate.
projects.next_milestone: Energize two new 345 kV substations (about 1.1 GW)
projects.key_risks: 345 kV substation timing, pending permits for the expansion, aquifer drawdown disputes, and a county move (Sept 22) to draft zoning barring new hyperscale campuses.

projects.name: AWS Madison County (Canton/Ridgeland)
projects.status_note: Five Canton buildings are running and buildings 6-9 have roofs on. The Ridgeland campus is in early construction after an $11-12B expansion was announced in April 2026.
projects.power_source: Entergy Mississippi grid with new Entergy gas plants and solar; 616 MW of Amazon renewable contracts; diesel backup (800+ generators)
projects.cooling: Air cooling most of the year, water about 9% of the year
projects.water_source: Canton municipal, moving to recycled wastewater in 2027; Ridgeland city water
projects.cost_note: $10B (2024) plus $11B (April 2026). MW are Epoch IT estimates for Canton only.
projects.next_milestone: Canton buildings 6-7 online; switch to recycled wastewater
projects.key_risks: Resident complaints about diesel generator noise and emissions; criticism of Entergy's confidential contract and cost recovery; water supply concerns.

projects.name: AWS Salem Twp (Susquehanna)
projects.status_note: The 1,200-acre campus has been under active construction since October 2025 around a 48 MW building Talen finished in 2023; new-building commissioning dates are TBD.
projects.power_source: Susquehanna nuclear plant (Talen) under a 1,920 MW PPA, moving to front-of-meter grid delivery
projects.cooling: Outside air most of the year, direct evaporative under 2% of the year
projects.water_source: Onsite well and Susquehanna River withdrawal plus municipal; SRBC approved
projects.cost_note: Amazon paid $650M for the campus; $20B is AWS's statewide PA pledge with no site cost. 1,920 MW is PPA volume ramping to 2032.
projects.next_milestone: Commission first Amazon-built buildings; NPDES cooling-water discharge permit
projects.key_risks: FERC earlier rejected expanding behind-the-meter supply; objections to cooling-water discharge to the Susquehanna; reactor licenses (2042/2044) cap long-term supply.

projects.name: AWS Energy Way (Richmond County)
projects.status_note: Construction on the 21-building, roughly 800-acre campus was visible by September 2026. NC DEQ issued air permits Aug 28 for Duke's temporary bridge-power engines and Amazon's backup engines; operations expected early 2027.
projects.power_source: Duke Energy Progress grid; 57 diesel bridge-power engines for about a year; 588 diesel backup engines
projects.cooling: Air cooling most of the year, water on the hottest days
projects.water_source: Not disclosed
projects.cost_note: $10B announced initial investment.
projects.next_milestone: Initial operations on Duke bridge power
projects.key_risks: Possible appeal of the air permits by SELC; organized local opposition; uncertain grid interconnection timing.

projects.name: AWS Butts County (Project Lighthouse)
projects.status_note: Early construction in River Park Industrial Park near I-75 with 12-14 buildings planned and the first targeted for 2027.
projects.power_source: Not disclosed
projects.cooling: Not disclosed
projects.water_source: Butts County Water and Sewer Authority
projects.cost_note: $11B is AWS's combined Butts and Douglas county figure. Unverified trackers cite about 786 MW.
projects.next_milestone: First building energized; PILOT payments begin
projects.key_risks: Capacity, power and water undisclosed; depends on new Georgia Power and transmission buildout and water/sewer upgrades.

projects.name: Homer City Energy Campus
projects.status_note: Vertical construction of the 4.5 GW gas plant began April 2026. AWS filed for 36 data-center buildings in phases from December 2026; the county planning commission tabled it in September.
projects.power_source: Onsite 4.4-4.5 GW gas plant (seven GE Vernova 7HA.02 turbines, Marcellus gas), over 1 GW exported to grid
projects.cooling: Not described for the data halls
projects.water_source: Former power station's existing water-withdrawal rights
projects.cost_note: $10B developer figure for campus and power plant; AWS building costs undisclosed. Planned MW is the ~3,700 MW of the 4.5 GW plant reportedly reserved for data centers.
projects.next_milestone: County decision on AWS preliminary plan; AWS phase 1 start
projects.key_risks: Air permits appealed to the Environmental Hearing Board; resident opposition (AWS plan tabled); schedule depends on turbine deliveries; very large value accumulation beside one dedicated plant.

projects.name: Google Pryor (MidAmerica Ind. Park)
projects.status_note: Running since 2011 and still growing; a converted warehouse building came online in early September 2026. The Pryor share of Google's $9B 2025 Oklahoma pledge is undisclosed.
projects.power_source: GRDA grid (Grand River Energy Center) via new on-campus substation
projects.cooling: Evaporative cooling towers (64 units, about 484 MW heat rejection)
projects.water_source: Neosho River via MidAmerica Industrial Park water system
projects.cost_note: Epoch AI estimate for the AI-compute portion (368 MW IT). Google says about $15B invested in Oklahoma since 2007.
projects.next_milestone: Pryor scope of the $9B Oklahoma investment built out
projects.key_risks: Heavy evaporative water draw (over 1.1B gallons in FY2025); new large-load cost rules under Oklahoma HB 2992.

projects.name: Google Stillwater
projects.status_note: Phase 1 lots are platted and permitted with building started on the first two. The OG&E power contract covering this campus and two Muskogee sites awaits OCC approval.
projects.power_source: OG&E grid plus two Google-backed solar farms under construction
projects.cooling: Not disclosed (about 3B gal/yr projected water use suggests water-based cooling)
projects.water_source: City of Stillwater municipal (Kaw Lake)
projects.cost_note: Earlier reported figure of up to $3B. Three OG&E-served sites (Stillwater and Muskogee) ramp to about 1 GW over 5 years with no per-site split.
projects.next_milestone: OCC ruling on OG&E-Google service agreements
projects.key_risks: Depends on OCC approval of the OG&E contract and large-load tariff; large municipal water commitment.

projects.name: Google West Memphis
projects.status_note: Ground broken October 2025 on a five-building campus with an 18-24 month build; regulators approved the supporting Entergy solar project in March 2026.
projects.power_source: Entergy Arkansas grid plus new 600 MW solar and 350 MW battery storage; onsite substation
projects.cooling: Graywater reuse plant for cooling; system type not specified
projects.water_source: Onsite graywater reuse plant
projects.cost_note: Google's announced $4B Arkansas investment through 2027.
projects.next_milestone: First building completed
projects.key_risks: Depends on Entergy's new solar and storage; pending Army Corps review of the floodplain site; 30-year PILOT deal under scrutiny.

projects.name: Project Tembo (Cheyenne)
projects.developer: Google (Jupiter Star Holdings); power by Tallgrass
projects.status_note: Crusoe exited in June 2026 and a Google subsidiary filed an amended site plan for a 2.7 GW four-hall campus. Tallgrass says its power hub is proceeding; utility service targeted early 2028.
projects.power_source: Tallgrass Cheyenne Power Hub (about 2.7 GW new gas, Mitsubishi M501JAC), plus fuel cells and Black Hills grid
projects.cooling: Not disclosed
projects.water_source: Not disclosed
projects.cost_note: No campus cost reported; about $7B is Tallgrass's power-hub investment.
projects.next_milestone: Power hub and utility service for first operations
projects.key_risks: Developer change raised cost and schedule concerns; resident objections to water use and gas emissions; long-lead turbine deliveries.

projects.name: Lake Mariner (Fluidstack/Anthropic)
projects.status_note: The first Fluidstack building began running for Anthropic around May 2026; a second is nearly finished and a third is being fitted out at this former coal-plant site on Lake Ontario.
projects.power_source: Grid (NYISO); former coal plant site
projects.cooling: Dry coolers, non-evaporative closed loop
projects.water_source: Not disclosed
projects.cost_note: Epoch AI projection for the Anthropic buildings. 360 MW is contracted critical IT.
projects.next_milestone: Building CB-4 energized
projects.key_risks: Third building running about a quarter late per Epoch; tied to Fluidstack financing and a Google backstop; site transmission caps expansion.

projects.name: Barber Lake (Fluidstack/Anthropic)
projects.status_note: The first building's shell, chillers and generators were mostly installed by mid-2026 but not energized. Cipher extended the lease to 20 years; first halls due late 2026 to early 2027.
projects.power_source: ERCOT grid with about 120 diesel backup generators
projects.cooling: Air-cooled chillers (about 175 units)
projects.water_source: Onsite supply (no city water)
projects.cost_note: Epoch AI projection at 207 MW critical IT (about 300 MW gross).
projects.next_milestone: First data hall delivered and rent starts
projects.key_risks: About three months behind schedule and over budget; fragile town water system, prompting a $10M repair pledge.

projects.name: Project Thunderbird (Enid)
projects.status_note: Proposed September 2026 as four campuses around Enid on about 1,750 acres; rezoning filed for two sites, with no city water agreement and no tenant yet.
projects.power_source: Behind-the-meter gas plant up to 3.3 GW; not grid-supplied
projects.cooling: Closed-loop recirculating
projects.water_source: Raw water from Kaw Lake pipeline (agreement pending)
projects.cost_note: Developer's estimate of up to $35B. 2.75 GW is IT load.
projects.next_milestone: Rezoning hearings (planning commission and city commission)
projects.key_risks: Needs zoning, a water deal, a tenant, financing and air permits for a 3.3 GW gas plant; organized local opposition.

projects.name: IREN Project Emerald (Kiowa)
projects.status_note: IREN owns part of the roughly 2,000-acre site and a county committee endorsed the tax-incentive plan; commissioners have not voted on the TIF districts and a public-vote petition is being prepared.
projects.power_source: PSO grid interconnection (studies complete)
projects.cooling: Closed-loop recirculating (per IREN)
projects.water_source: Not disclosed
projects.cost_note: About $50B across two phases per county documents; capacity figures conflict (1.6 GW vs 1.2 GW per phase).
projects.next_milestone: County commissioners vote on TIF districts
projects.key_risks: TIF not approved and abatement may face a public vote; uncertain local water; no signed tenant.

projects.name: Fermi Project Matador (Amarillo)
projects.tenant: TensorWave (first lease, 222 MW, options to 650 MW)
projects.status_note: Site and power-plant groundwork is under way for six Siemens SGT-800 turbines. A first lease with TensorWave was signed in August 2026 but closing depends on financing; nothing in service yet.
projects.power_source: Private onsite grid: gas turbines plus a proposed 2.6 GW gas plant, four planned AP1000 nuclear units, solar and batteries
projects.cooling: Not specified (company claims about 80% less water than conventional)
projects.water_source: City of Amarillo (up to 2.5 MGD) plus Ogallala-region groundwater leases
projects.cost_note: Midpoint of a reported $70-90B+ estimate. Planned MW is the stated up-to-11 GW project; generation plans have grown to about 17 GW.
projects.next_milestone: TensorWave lease closing and project financing
projects.key_risks: No revenue and dependent on new capital; CEO firing litigation and a securities class action; air-permit challenges; Ogallala water scrutiny; unlicensed nuclear plans.

projects.name: Applied Digital Polaris Forge 1
projects.status_note: Two buildings are live with 250 MW of critical IT (building 2's second phase on Oct 1, 2026); a third 150 MW building is under construction.
projects.power_source: Regional grid (excess transmission capacity)
projects.cooling: Closed-loop (company general description)
projects.water_source: Not disclosed
projects.cost_note: No total cost reported; $1.59B of notes fund the third building. MW are critical IT.
projects.next_milestone: Third 150 MW building ready for service
projects.key_risks: Heavy debt load and single-tenant dependence on CoreWeave; note amortization tied to lease start makes delays costly.

projects.name: CoreWeave Lancaster
projects.developer: Chirisa / Machine Investment Group (JV with Blue Owl)
projects.status_note: Phase one converts a former printing plant; July 2026 imagery showed rooftop cooling going in but not yet running. Phase two needs city planning approval.
projects.power_source: PPL grid via new substation and switchyard; backup generators
projects.cooling: Rooftop air-cooled chillers
projects.water_source: Not disclosed (SRBC caps about 20,000 gal/day per site)
projects.cost_note: $6B CoreWeave commitment; 100 MW initial scalable to 300 MW.
projects.next_milestone: Building 1 operational (about 92 MW IT)
projects.key_risks: City zoning appeals, phase-two approval, and PPL substation timing.

projects.name: Prince William Digital Gateway
projects.status_note: Dead: courts voided the rezoning (affirmed March 2026) and QTS withdrew its last appeal on July 2, 2026.
projects.power_source: Not disclosed
projects.cooling: Not disclosed
projects.water_source: Not disclosed
projects.cost_note: QTS had claimed tens of billions for about 23M sq ft.
projects.next_milestone: None
projects.key_risks: Any revival needs new rezoning against strong battlefield-preservation opposition; county cut its by-right data-center district by two-thirds on Sept 25.

news.headline: Cipher doubled lease terms at its 300 MW Colorado City campus to 20 years, lifting contracted revenue above $9B; halls now due Q4 2026 to Q1 2027.
news.why_it_matters: Long leases support project debt, but shifted handover dates and overrun-sharing terms signal schedule pressure during commissioning.

news.headline: A $366M first building, reportedly tied to Anthropic, was filed near Austin with up to 710 MW of simple-cycle gas turbines planned on site.
news.why_it_matters: Behind-the-meter simple-cycle fleets put turbine breakdown, fuel supply and fire exposures together on one site.

news.headline: Raleigh's council voted 7-1 to pause approvals of large data centers for six months while it drafts new rules.
news.why_it_matters: More local pauses across the Southeast add permitting and schedule risk to projects still in planning.

news.headline: The Memphis council's data-center moratorium vote collapsed into protests and a fight and was pushed to October 20.
news.why_it_matters: The outcome could restrict further builds near the Colossus sites.

news.headline: Google signed for 3.6 GW from Constellation, including a 20-year 890 MW nuclear PPA tied to $4.3B of upgrades at 11 reactors.
news.why_it_matters: Uprate and life-extension work at operating nuclear units adds construction and operational exposure to nuclear and power books.

news.headline: AWS filed plans for 36 two-story buildings on 1,100 acres at Homer City, powered mainly by the 4.5 GW gas plant under construction next door.
news.why_it_matters: A very large value accumulation beside one dedicated plant makes power-loss business interruption the central question.

news.headline: TeraWulf doubled its Kentucky Power service agreement to 1 GW and pulled the second 500 MW phase forward to 2029.
news.why_it_matters: Delivery hinges on a new 765/345 kV substation and regulator approval: a single-point grid dependency.

news.headline: Applied Digital finished Building 2 at its CoreWeave-leased Ellendale campus, bringing live IT load to 250 MW of a planned 400 MW.
news.why_it_matters: Phased energization puts live halls beside active construction, mixing hot work and commissioning with operating exposure.

news.headline: Crusoe filed two satellite buildings worth $4.8B in Kent County, taking its Childress-linked Project Hyper to about $12B.
news.why_it_matters: Remote West Texas sites with limited fire service and severe convective storm exposure, carrying multibillion-dollar builder's risk values.

news.headline: We Energies reached a deal to supply the Oracle campus in Port Washington partly with output from Point Beach nuclear plant.
news.why_it_matters: Adds a firm supply leg, but the campus still cannot run until its new transmission line is approved.

news.headline: Governor Spanberger's executive order bans project NDAs and orders reviews of diesel backup generator impacts and new noise rules.
news.why_it_matters: Tighter diesel limits could change emergency power design and fuel storage in the largest US market.

news.headline: A 57-43 Senate vote fell short of cloture on a House-passed bill making data centers pay full grid-upgrade costs.
news.why_it_matters: Cost allocation stays a state-by-state patchwork, so tariff and collateral terms vary by site.

news.headline: Amazon signed a 20-year deal for 690 MW from Calvert Cliffs nuclear plant, backing more than $3B of upgrades and about 190 MW of new output.
news.why_it_matters: Hyperscaler-funded nuclear uprates bring large outage-and-upgrade construction exposure to operating plants.

news.headline: Valar Atomics applied to BLM for a Carbon County campus of about 456 small reactors, up to 9.6 GW, with fuel and waste facilities.
news.why_it_matters: Would co-locate unproven Gen IV reactors with data halls at a scale no nuclear pool has written.

news.headline: A weak tornado touched down among wind turbines about four miles from a Google data-center build in the Panhandle, causing no damage.
news.why_it_matters: A near miss that shows Panhandle campuses' tornado exposure.

news.headline: FERC suspended PJM's 6.8 GW emergency backstop capacity auction until February 2027, citing cost-allocation and collateral flaws.
news.why_it_matters: PJM's capacity shortfall persists, raising curtailment risk for Mid-Atlantic data centers.

news.headline: Prince William supervisors cut the county's by-right data-center district by about two-thirds, to 3,500 acres.
news.why_it_matters: Sites outside the smaller zone now face full review, slowing Northern Virginia pipelines.

news.headline: Applied Digital sited its $3.2B, 210 MW hyperscaler campus on 1,300 acres near Brookwood in Tuscaloosa County, opening 2028.
news.why_it_matters: A new multibillion-dollar build in a county with significant wind and convective storm exposure.

news.headline: Oracle sent Blue Owl a force-majeure notice after the gas pipeline for the 2.45 GW campus slipped to February 2027.
news.why_it_matters: Fuel-supply delays for onsite fuel-cell power are triggering contract relief: a clear delay-in-start-up warning.

news.headline: DOE picked 31 reconductoring and grid-upgrade projects for $1.9B, aiming to free about 23 GW of transfer capacity for large loads.
news.why_it_matters: Transmission helps interconnection but adds no generation, so onsite power stays the norm.

news.headline: Reporting shows El Paso Electric considered only gas to power Meta's campus, as a ruling on the dedicated 366 MW plant nears.
news.why_it_matters: A PUC denial or restriction would leave the 1 GW campus short of firm power.

news.headline: Governor Abbott froze new state environmental permits for data centers until ERCOT finishes its large-load audit, expected in December.
news.why_it_matters: Air permits for onsite turbines are on hold, putting a large share of the Texas pipeline at risk of delay.

news.headline: Newsom signed seven bills creating rate classes for 25 MW+ loads, requiring sworn water-use reporting and ending blanket CEQA exemptions.
news.why_it_matters: Water and energy disclosure will shape cooling choices and permit timelines in California.

news.headline: The county council voted 6-3 to start drafting zoning that would bar new hyperscale campuses; a final vote is expected within 60 days.
news.why_it_matters: The county hosts about 40 Amazon and Microsoft buildings, so future expansions face headwinds.

news.headline: New Era signed a 20-year PPA with Vistra's Luminant for at least 207 MW from the adjacent 1.1 GW Odessa gas plant.
news.why_it_matters: Supply from one neighboring plant concentrates outage risk; contingent business interruption needs review.

news.headline: Residents and an environmental group sued to void tax abatements and a land sale for a 3.2 GW OpenAI-linked campus, alleging secret dealings.
news.why_it_matters: A successful open-meetings challenge could unwind incentives and delay a coastal Georgia gigawatt build.

news.headline: Salem adopted an extendable 120-day data-center moratorium, halting phase one of Verrus's $5.1B campus.
news.why_it_matters: Shows local action can strand construction schedules and financing mid-stream.

permits.action: Mayor announces 90-day executive-order review of xAI guardrails
permits.summary: Mayor Paul Young said he would sign an executive order starting a 90-day review of guardrails for xAI covering land use, infrastructure, air, water and aquifer, utility costs and noise, separate from the council's moratorium debate.
permits.schedule_impact: May lead to new city conditions on xAI's Memphis operations and expansion once the 90 days end.

permits.action: Final vote on data center moratorium postponed again
permits.summary: On October 6, 2026, the Memphis City Council voted seven to five, with one member absent, to delay for a second time its final decision on a proposed data center moratorium, pushing the vote to October 20.
permits.schedule_impact: Whether Memphis adopts a citywide pause on data centers remains undecided; the source does not describe the ordinance's terms.

permits.action: Rezoning vote pulled from Oct 6 agenda; special meeting set
permits.summary: The city took the rezoning items off the October 6 agenda to find a bigger venue, then scheduled a special 5 p.m. meeting and public hearing on October 27 at Stride Bank Center, where the commission will approve or deny them.
permits.schedule_impact: The binding zoning decision slips about three weeks, to October 27.

permits.action: Oracle subscription to Point Beach nuclear output
permits.summary: We Energies announced a deal for Oracle to take 10% to 20% of Point Beach nuclear output for the Lighthouse campus, which needs PSC approval; on the same day it filed for a new gas plant at the Fox Energy Center.
permits.schedule_impact: Adds a power supply source for the campus if the PSC approves it.

permits.action: Planning commission recommends the three Thunderbird rezonings
permits.summary: After a public hearing, the Enid MAPC voted to send favorable recommendations on all three rezoning requests to the City Commission, which makes the final decision.
permits.schedule_impact: Clears the advisory step, so the rezoning now goes to the City Commission for a binding vote.

permits.agency: St. Joseph County Council / Area Plan Commission
permits.action: Council votes 6-3 to draft ban on new hyperscale campuses
permits.summary: The county council voted 6-3 on a resolution telling the Area Plan Commission to amend zoning to stop additional hyperscale data centers; the measure is expected back before the council for a final vote within about 60 days. A sponsor said it is not technically a ban.
permits.schedule_impact: Could stop new hyperscale projects in the county. How already-approved or under-construction projects (Amazon in New Carlisle, Microsoft in Granger) would be treated has not been decided.

permits.agency: Prince William Board of County Supervisors
permits.action: Shrinks data center overlay; new sites need special use permit
permits.summary: Prince William County supervisors adopted a zoning text amendment (Ord. No. 26-67) that limits the Data Center Opportunity Zone Overlay District to parcels meeting set eligibility pathways, closes it to future expansion, and requires a special use permit for new data center proposals in listed business, office and industrial districts outside it; the final eligibility period closes Dec. 21, 2026, after which an updated boundary map will be published.
permits.schedule_impact: New data center proposals in the listed business, office and industrial districts outside the overlay must now go through the special use permit process, and the overlay can no longer grow, so fresh filings in those districts face added review.

permits.agency: Lancaster County Court of Common Pleas
permits.action: Judge stays zoning board hearing on residents' phase 2 appeal
permits.summary: Lancaster RAGE appealed the city planning commission's July 1 conditional approval of the second building. A county judge, Thomas Sponaugle, granted the developers' emergency request to halt the scheduled zoning hearing while their court action seeking to dismiss the appeal goes forward.
permits.schedule_impact: Freezes the residents' challenge for now. A ruling for the developers, like the 2025 ruling on an earlier appeal, would clear phase 2's path to final approval.

permits.agency: Office of the Governor of Texas / Texas Commission on Environmental Quality
permits.action: TCEQ ordered to halt all data-center permit issuance
permits.summary: Abbott ordered TCEQ to issue no permits sought by data centers until ERCOT's audit is finished. Law-firm analysis says this covers NSR air and TPDES wastewater permits statewide, including islanded behind-the-meter projects outside ERCOT. Sources date the directive September 21; commentary on it appeared September 23.
permits.schedule_impact: Blocks new air and water permits, such as Fermi's pending 5 GW application, likely until ERCOT's audit ends around mid-December 2026. TCEQ owes the governor a compliance update by October 19.

permits.agency: Office of the Governor of Virginia
permits.action: Executive Order 22 sets Virginia Data Center Accountability Framework
permits.summary: The order took effect on signing, September 18, 2026. State economic-development assistance, including the Business Ready Sites program and expedited permitting programs, may not go to new data centers expecting peak demand of 25 MW or more. Executive-branch agencies may not enter or enforce nondisclosure agreements that hide material information about proposed data centers; existing commitments are honored. DEQ must expedite noise and cooling-water-scarcity rules and review backup generators. The Chief Energy Officer's office is told to work with utilities, the SCC and PJM on shielding households from data-center grid costs.
permits.schedule_impact: Removes state fast-track assistance for new data centers of 25 MW or more. DEQ owes timelines, workplans and findings on noise, backup generators and cooling-water scarcity within 180 days.
permits.source: Office of the Governor of Virginia

permits.action: Petitions against air hearing and emergency well denied; stays lifted
permits.summary: The court rejected New Energy Economy's petition on the air permit proceeding and the Center for Biological Diversity's petition over a new well drilled without a public hearing, and ended the stays it imposed on Aug 23.
permits.schedule_impact: Let well water use and the air permit case resume after about a month's pause.

permits.action: Draft significant permit modification: two new generators
permits.summary: IDEM opened a 30-day comment period on SPM 141-50312-00650, which would add two generators, modify existing ones and revise permit conditions.
permits.schedule_impact: Generator additions for further buildings wait on the final modification.

permits.agency: Office of the Governor of Texas / Texas Water Development Board
permits.action: TWDB told to enforce water-use reporting by data centers
permits.summary: Abbott directed the TWDB to enforce water-use reporting requirements against major water users, including data centers, alongside an ERCOT state-and-community-impact RFI.
permits.schedule_impact: Campuses that miss water surveys can be flagged to the PUCT and the governor, and compliance feeds into when the permit pause lifts.

permits.action: Planning commission recommends ending by-right data centers
permits.summary: On a 5-3 vote, the commission recommended a zoning text amendment ending by-right data centers. It also recommended a 120-day filing window and a 500-foot setback from homes and schools.
permits.schedule_impact: Sent the overlay rollback to the Board of County Supervisors for a September 22 vote.

permits.action: Citizen petition seeks charter ban on large data centers
permits.summary: Johnstown residents submitted a petition, with enough validated signatures, for a city charter amendment (new Section 10.07) that would bar certain data centers and any exceeding 25 megawatts of combined monthly demand, though timing made the Nov. 3 ballot unlikely without quick council action.
permits.schedule_impact: If adopted, it would bar certain data centers and any above 25 megawatts of combined monthly demand in Johnstown, in Licking County; the source does not tie it to the Meta campus and does not say what happened after the Sept 4 council deadline.

permits.action: ATC submits revised Ozaukee County interconnection application (137-CE-229)
permits.summary: ATC's project page says a revised application went to the PSC in September 2026. It drops the earlier east-west route through parts of Trenton and Saukville; the Contingent Route remains part of the alternate South West Route.
permits.schedule_impact: PSC approval is listed as to be determined. ATC expects to start construction about 31 days after the PSC's written order and to be in service about 17 months after construction begins.

permits.action: Advocates appeal PSC's Meta subpoena ruling in state court
permits.summary: Represented by Earthjustice, the Alliance for Affordable Energy and Union of Concerned Scientists asked the district court in late September to reverse the PSC's August decision as arbitrary and reinstate the subpoena.
permits.schedule_impact: If the court reinstates the subpoena, discovery could reopen in the seven-plant case and push back its final vote.

permits.action: ALJs recommend conditional approval of McCloud plant
permits.summary: After a July hearing, administrative law judges issued a proposed decision finding El Paso Electric had not properly studied alternatives or run an RFP, and recommended approval only if ratepayers bear none of the capital or operating costs, otherwise denial; no commission vote had been set.
permits.schedule_impact: The five commissioners make the final decision on whether and on what cost terms the plant is approved; no vote date had been set as of the article.

permits.action: ALJ orally recommends approving OG&E–Google settlement
permits.summary: At a September 2026 hearing, the ALJ urged commissioners to approve the settlement. Nobody testified against it, and the Oklahoma Industrial Energy Consumers said it would not oppose. Under the settlement, OG&E must report any broader grid upgrades within 30 days so that cost allocation can be decided later. The recommendation was oral, not a written order.
permits.schedule_impact: A final commission order is still needed; no vote date has been reported.

permits.action: Entergy rate case session to probe Google-related buildout
permits.summary: Records released under FOIA show Google paying about $526M toward Cypress Solar and $190M for transmission upgrades. Entergy's pending base-rate case, opposed by Walmart and other businesses, comes before commissioners at a Nov 4–5 session. The date of this item is the date the payment figures were reported.
permits.schedule_impact: Commissioners could scrutinize who pays for the Google-related generation and transmission.

permits.agency: Wyoming regulator (not named in Black Hills release)
permits.action: South Cheyenne Transmission Expansion CPCN filed
permits.summary: Black Hills filed for a certificate for the South Cheyenne Transmission Expansion in September 2026. A further Wyoming transmission expansion CPCN is planned for Q4 2026.
permits.schedule_impact: Transmission approval timing could affect the late-2027 energization and the ramp to peak load by 2030.

permits.action: Commission review begins of OG&E–Google service agreements (Cause 2026-000031)
permits.summary: In September 2026, an administrative law judge was set to begin review of OG&E's electric service agreements to serve three Google data centers in Muskogee and Stillwater. Google pays all grid-connection costs and contracted costs regardless of usage, and plans solar generation from two arrays under construction. Commission staff testimony supported the agreements.
permits.schedule_impact: The agreements cannot take effect without formal commission approval.

permits.action: Starts curative amendment process on data centers
permits.summary: East Lampeter Township in Lancaster County began the process of adopting a curative amendment to address data centers; the report gives no further details.
permits.schedule_impact: Shows a neighboring township moving to regulate data centers; the effect on the city campus is not described.

permits.action: Starts curative amendment on data centers; vote possible December
permits.summary: East Hempfield Township in Lancaster County began adopting a curative amendment on data centers, with a vote possible as soon as December.
permits.schedule_impact: Adds another Lancaster-area township with pending data center limits; no direct link to the city campus is reported.

permits.action: Allows data centers in general industrial zone by conditional use
permits.summary: West Hempfield Township in Lancaster County voted to allow data centers only in its general industrial district with conditional use approval, capping buildings at 120,000 square feet (156,000 with a 75% green roof).
permits.schedule_impact: Caps data center size and adds conditional use review in this Lancaster-area township; no direct effect on the city campus is reported.

permits.action: Enacts 12-month moratorium on data center permits
permits.summary: Newton Falls Village Council voted 4-0 on an emergency basis for a 12-month moratorium on data center permits to give officials time to research data centers, with one member citing Lordstown's court fight over a data center as a reason to prepare.
permits.schedule_impact: Closes another neighboring community to new data center permits for a year, which may matter for any related development near the Lordstown site.

permits.action: Approves one-year moratorium on larger data center projects
permits.summary: Warren City Council unanimously approved a one-year moratorium on data center projects over 1,000 square feet and directed the mayor to form a Data Center Review Committee that must deliver recommendations within nine months.
permits.schedule_impact: The city is pausing new data center projects over 1,000 square feet for a year while a review committee prepares recommendations; the source does not tie it to the Lordstown campus.

permits.agency: Laramie County Board of County Commissioners
permits.action: Rezoned 1,835 acres to PUD for Vantage Project Latigo
permits.summary: Laramie County commissioners unanimously rezoned a 1,835-acre site along Terry Ranch Road, about 12 miles south of Cheyenne, from LU to PUD for Vantage's 480 MW Project Latigo data center campus, which plans onsite power generation and construction-worker accommodation.
permits.schedule_impact: The county board approved the rezoning for Vantage's planned campus south of Cheyenne; Vantage called it one of the first entitlement and permitting steps, so more approvals remain.

permits.action: Approves rezoning for Terra Nexus data center
permits.summary: The Rockingham City Council voted 4-1 to approve a rezoning for a Terra Nexus data center on Old Cheraw Highway in Rockingham, North Carolina, which the city has described as a $1.2 billion investment.
permits.schedule_impact: The approval lets the Terra Nexus project move forward; no groundbreaking timeline was given.

permits.agency: NC DEQ Division of Air Quality
permits.action: Final permit for 588 AWS emergency backup engines
permits.summary: NC DEQ's Division of Air Quality announced final permits for Amazon Data Services' 588 emergency backup engines at its Energy Way Tech Campus on Airport Road in Hamlet, Richmond County. After public comment, the Amazon permit clarifies fuel-use monitoring and both permits add recordkeeping and reporting requirements.
permits.schedule_impact: Final permits for the campus backup engines were announced Aug 28, 2026; the release does not discuss appeals.

permits.agency: NC DEQ Division of Air Quality
permits.action: Final permit for Duke's 57 bridge-power engines
permits.summary: DAQ issued a final permit for Duke Energy Progress to run 57 temporary bridge-power engines in Richmond County to supply Amazon's facility until it connects to the grid. The final permit adds more initial generator testing, limits the bridge power to Amazon's facility, and requires Duke to retire the engines within a year of starting operation. DAQ also issued Amazon's permit for 588 emergency backup engines.
permits.schedule_impact: Provides temporary power to Amazon's facility until it connects to the grid; the engines must be retired within a year of starting operation.

permits.action: Plainsmen Holdings files three agricultural-to-industrial rezoning applications
permits.summary: Plainsmen Holdings asked the city to rezone the North Campus and part of the West Campus from agricultural to I-3, and another West Campus tract from agricultural to I-2.
permits.schedule_impact: Nothing can move to development agreements or permitting until the City Commission approves these rezonings.
permits.source: City of Enid – Project Thunderbird page

permits.action: Further draft construction permit modification; comments closed
permits.summary: MDEQ's records for the Amazon Madison Mega Site in Canton list a draft air construction permit modification (1720-00098) whose public comment period ends August 24, 2026; no final action is shown.
permits.schedule_impact: Final action on the draft modification has not yet been shown in MDEQ's records.

permits.action: Council members propose two-year pause on new data centers
permits.summary: Five Republican St. Joseph County Council members and candidates proposed a two-year pause on new data centers, which would first go to the Area Plan Commission for a public hearing, to look at the effects of the two hyperscale projects already underway before approving more.
permits.schedule_impact: If adopted, it would pause new data center approvals in St. Joseph County; supporters say they would need five council votes after November's election, and no hearing or vote date has been set.

permits.action: Adopts zoning code limits on data center noise and proximity
permits.summary: Olive Branch, Mississippi officials codified new zoning language on August 18, 2026, effective immediately, that restricts data center noise and how close data centers can be to homes; previously they were allowed by right in industrial zones under the storage-warehouse definition.
permits.schedule_impact: Officials said they wanted to avoid situations like those in Memphis and Southaven involving SpaceXAI, pointing to tighter siting rules for new data centers in Olive Branch.

permits.action: Denies Amazon's property valuation appeal for Canton buildings
permits.summary: Supervisors kept the assessor's value of about $292 million per building for five Canton data centers, rejecting Amazon's proposed value of about $69 million, though Amazon can still go to court.
permits.schedule_impact: Protects about $5.8 million in county revenue this year, but a court appeal could reopen the FILOT valuation basis.

permits.action: Oracle moves to dismiss its suit against PSC credit rules
permits.summary: Oracle sued in Ozaukee County Circuit Court in June 2026 to set aside the PSC's credit-rating requirements for data center developers, then its attorneys filed a motion to voluntarily dismiss on Aug 17, 2026.
permits.schedule_impact: The credit rules now stand unchallenged in court. Oracle's S&P rating of BBB- is below the PSC's A- threshold, so it could face over $100 million a year in financial security for the Port Washington data center.

permits.action: Hearing on conditional use permit PZ-26-00057 for office complex
permits.summary: A Class B conditional use permit (PZ-26-00057) and commercial site plan for an office complex east of Switchgrass Industrial Park, next to US 85, were set for a Planning Commission public hearing on Aug 13, 2026. The memo does not report the outcome.
permits.schedule_impact: If approved, the office complex can be built alongside the data center.
permits.source: Laramie County Board of Commissioners memo

permits.action: PSC overturns ALJ order compelling Meta disclosures
permits.summary: By a 3-1 vote the commission reversed an administrative law judge's interlocutory ruling that would have made Meta produce investment, job and load data for the U-37882 case, which made Meta's motion to quash the subpoena moot.
permits.schedule_impact: Kept the seven-plant docket on its fast schedule; the ruling is now under court challenge.

permits.action: County reviews Citizens booster station and tanks for LEAP water
permits.summary: At an August public hearing, county planners criticized Citizens' booster station and storage tanks for the LEAP water line, which Citizens moved there after Whitestown denied a variance, but they said they control development standards and not location; site plan review is expected October 13.
permits.schedule_impact: Delays to this site plan could slow the pipeline that supplies water to Meta and Lilly in the LEAP district.

permits.action: TCEQ notice of application and preliminary decision for Crusoe's Abilene power generation air permits
permits.summary: Crusoe Technologies applied on Nov 7, 2025 for air permits 182126, PSDTX1688 and GHGPSDTX263 to build an electric power generation facility at 615 FM 2404 in Abilene. TCEQ's notice of application and preliminary decision carries an issuance date of Aug 5, 2026.
permits.schedule_impact: Written requests for a contested case hearing are allowed within 30 days of the notice for permits 182126 and PSDTX1688 (not the greenhouse gas permit), so the permits are not final yet.
permits.source: TCEQ (Notice of Application and Preliminary Decision)

permits.agency: Interconnection approval authority (not named in source)
permits.action: TeraWulf pursues 250 MW more power at Lake Mariner, subject to interconnection approval
permits.summary: In its Q2 2026 results, TeraWulf said it is pursuing 250 MW of additional power capacity at its New York platform, subject to interconnection approval, and gave no timeline. Construction continues on 336 MW across CB-4 and CB-5, with CB-5 targeted to begin phased delivery in early 2027. The date is the results announcement, not a filing date.
permits.schedule_impact: Growth beyond the CB-4/CB-5 build depends on the interconnection approval the company mentions.

permits.agency: Office of the Governor of Texas / PUCT / ERCOT
permits.action: Audit and pause of data centers in ERCOT interconnection
permits.summary: Abbott ordered the PUCT and ERCOT to audit every data center moving through ERCOT interconnection and to hold their advancement until the audit is done. Projects must disclose financial assistance received, power use and on-site generation, water use and cooling, community-impact steps, and ownership and control.
permits.schedule_impact: Freezes interconnection progress for queued campuses until the audit ends. ERCOT's impact RFI responses are due October 12, and ERCOT expects to report around December 10, 2026.

permits.agency: Wyoming regulator (not named in Black Hills release)
permits.action: Air permit approved for Cheyenne Prairie generation expansion
permits.summary: Black Hills reports that the air quality permit for its Cheyenne Prairie generation expansion serving Google was approved in August 2026.
permits.schedule_impact: Removes an air-permitting hurdle for the utility-owned generation behind the campus.

permits.action: Directs staff to draft stopgap data center ordinance
permits.summary: Manheim Township in Lancaster County voted to have staff draft a stopgap ordinance that would require conditional use approval for data centers in its industrial zones.
permits.schedule_impact: Would put any data center growth in this neighboring township through a conditional use hearing; no direct effect on the city campus is reported.

permits.action: Sends proposed data center ordinance to planners
permits.summary: Manheim Borough in Lancaster County proposed allowing data centers in its industrial and planned industrial/corporate center districts with conditional use approval and sent the ordinance to borough and county planners, with a final vote tentatively set for Oct. 27.
permits.schedule_impact: Another Lancaster-area municipality setting a conditional use path for data centers; no direct effect on the city campus is reported.

permits.action: Adopts data center ordinance with 30-acre minimum lots
permits.summary: Pequea Township in Lancaster County adopted an ordinance limiting data centers to lots of 30-plus acres in its commercial and industrial districts, with conditional use approval and 300-foot setbacks from homes and schools.
permits.schedule_impact: Adds large-lot and setback limits on data centers in a Lancaster-area township; no direct effect on the city campus is reported.

permits.action: Drafts temporary data center moratorium and zoning rules
permits.summary: Warren Township's zoning commission, noting the township has no data center zoning rules, is working toward a temporary moratorium and drafting language requiring data centers to meet township guidelines; one trustee said the trustee board had not discussed or decided on a moratorium.
permits.schedule_impact: If adopted, it would put a temporary pause on data centers in Warren Township; as of late August no decision had been made and the source does not tie it to the Lordstown campus.

permits.action: Voters overturn rezoning for proposed $1 billion data center
permits.summary: In the August primary, about 90% of Augusta Township voters overturned the Township Board of Trustees' rezoning for a proposed $1 billion data center, and residents have also filed petitions to recall all seven trustees.
permits.schedule_impact: The source does not mention the Saline campus; the vote shows strong voter opposition to a data center rezoning in this township.

permits.action: Sierra Club contests Meta campus minor-source air permit revision
permits.summary: Sierra Club told LDEQ that Meta affiliate Laidley's permit change, which adds 44 round-the-clock gas boilers to 31 diesel generators and was approved in June, puts the site over major-source thresholds, and it asked for a public hearing.
permits.schedule_impact: If LDEQ requires a major-source permit, the campus's on-site combustion equipment could face more review and delay.
permits.source: Louisiana Illuminator via News From The States

permits.action: MDEQ sets retirement schedule for 69 temporary xAI turbines
permits.summary: MDEQ issued an order on July 30, 2026 setting dates for xAI to retire 69 temporary turbines in Southaven, starting Aug 18. Most are to be retired by April 2027, 13 may run past the original 12-month limit, and turbines that began running in early July must stop by July 14, 2027.
permits.schedule_impact: Sets hard retirement dates for xAI's temporary Southaven turbines. xAI cited supply-chain delays for 41 permanent turbines that are to hold air permits.

permits.agency: Court of Appeals of Virginia / Prince William County
permits.action: Digital Gateway rezonings void; land reverts to prior zoning
permits.summary: When the stay ended, the Board's rezoning approvals became void and the land returned to its earlier zoning. On August 5, 2026, the county said it had updated the zoning maps and would reassess the parcels.
permits.schedule_impact: Takes away the data-center zoning, so any revived project would have to start a new land-use process.

permits.action: Green Chile lateral moved to full section 7 review (CP26-80)
permits.summary: Transwestern's January 2026 prior-notice request under its blanket certificate for the roughly 17.8-mile Green Chile pipeline drew a FERC staff protest over a missing state historic-preservation finding, so it proceeds as a full section 7 application. FERC scheduled its environmental assessment for Sept 4 and a federal authorization decision deadline of Dec 3.
permits.schedule_impact: Gas for the fuel-cell microgrid waits on this decision, and filings already put service at February 2027.

permits.action: ATC large-load commitment agreements and minimum transmission charge agreement filed at FERC
permits.summary: A July 24, 2026 transmittal letter, filed through MISO for ATC, asks FERC to accept four amended large-load project commitment agreements and a minimum transmission charge agreement, effective July 1, 2026, for a Microsoft data center campus in Racine County. Minimum charges begin when the transmission facilities enter service and run for 15 years.
permits.schedule_impact: FERC acceptance is needed for the agreements to take effect as filed; the letter asks for the 60-day notice requirement to be waived.

permits.action: Adopts framework requiring Special Permits for future hyperscale centers
permits.summary: El Paso City Council approved the city's first Data Center Policy Framework, under which future hyperscale data centers need a Special Permit with public notice, City Plan Commission review, a hearing and a Council vote, plus standards on water, energy, wastewater, noise, lighting and ecology.
permits.schedule_impact: KVIA reports the framework does not affect Meta's data center under construction in Northeast El Paso; the rules still have to be carried out through future ordinance amendments.

permits.action: Signed contract keeps plant-siting clause PSC struck; fix pending
permits.summary: Microsoft signed its 15-year Mount Pleasant service contract unchanged, including the eastern-Wisconsin/Upper Peninsula plant-location clause the PSC had removed, and We Energies says it will follow the order and correct the language with the PSC on no set timeline.
permits.schedule_impact: We Energies says it will follow the PSC order rather than the contract wording while it works with the commission to fix the language, with no timeline given.

permits.action: Approves industrial-zone data center rules with conditional use
permits.summary: Rapho Township in Lancaster County approved rules allowing data centers in its industrial zone through a conditional use hearing and requiring public water and sewer service.
permits.schedule_impact: Ties data center siting in this township to public water and sewer; no direct effect on the city campus is reported.

permits.action: Reconsideration of pipeline ROW denial rejected
permits.summary: The land commissioner refused Energy Transfer's request to reopen her denial of two rights-of-way and a lease for about 0.6 miles of pipeline across state land.
permits.schedule_impact: Keeps state trust land off the table for the gas route; the developer could still contest the decision administratively.

permits.action: Adopts first data center rules, 7-0
permits.summary: Lancaster City Council unanimously limited future data centers to the suburban manufacturing district (16 properties in the city's northeast), required a zoning hearing plus noise studies, setbacks and decommissioning plans, and set the rules to take effect Aug. 3.
permits.schedule_impact: The 216 Greenfield Road and 1375 Harrisburg Pike sites are exempt because their projects were already under way, but the rules make further data center sites in the city much harder to develop.

permits.action: Adopts six-month pause on data center zoning and permits
permits.summary: The Jackson City Council voted 5-2 on July 14, 2026 to impose a six-month moratorium on data center decisions, with an exception for the area next to Jackson-Medgar Evers Wiley International Airport; the city had earlier promised to delay data center zoning changes and permit approvals until it adopts regulations.
permits.schedule_impact: The pause covers only the City of Jackson for six months; the source does not link it to Madison County projects.

permits.action: Air permit for fuel-cell microgrid (NSR 10883)
permits.summary: NMED docketed a public hearing (AQB 26-57) on Yucca Growth Infrastructure's air permit application for the campus's fuel-cell microgrid, and its July 16 scheduling order set the hearing for Oct 19, 2026.
permits.schedule_impact: The microgrid that powers the campus has no air permit until this hearing and the decision after it are done; the August Supreme Court stay (lifted Sept 17) may have moved the hearing date.

permits.action: $4.8B valuation cap dropped from data center tax abatement
permits.summary: The township board voted 5-0 to remove a $4.8 billion valuation cap from its tax abatement for 'The Barn' after the township attorney warned the cap would violate a 2025 consent judgment. The clawback provision stays.
permits.schedule_impact: Resolves the consent-judgment conflict the attorney raised; the clawback provision remains in force.

permits.agency: U.S. District Court, Eastern District of Wisconsin
permits.action: Neighbors file noise class action against Microsoft
permits.summary: Three Sturtevant residents sued Microsoft in federal court on behalf of a proposed class of people living within 1.5 miles of its Fairwater data center in Mount Pleasant (over 1,000 households alleged), saying noise from cooling fans physically invades their properties.
permits.schedule_impact: No relief sought is described in the article, so any effect on operations is unknown.

permits.action: Industrial siting permit filed for Cheyenne Prairie gas expansion
permits.summary: Black Hills filed for an industrial siting permit in July 2026 to add 564 MW of new gas generation at its Cheyenne Prairie station. The plant will serve Google's Cheyenne data center, with about $1.8B to be spent in 2027–2029. The release does not name the agency; this permit type in Wyoming is issued by the Industrial Siting Council.
permits.schedule_impact: Black Hills plans to start construction in 2027, with energy service for Google planned to begin in late 2027.

permits.action: Conditional preliminary land-development approval for second Greenfield Rd building
permits.summary: The planning commission gave conditional preliminary land-development approval to a second data center building at 216 Greenfield Road. A resident group, Lancaster RAGE, appealed the approval; developers sued to throw out the appeal, and a judge stayed the zoning hearing.
permits.schedule_impact: The approval is under resident appeal, and the zoning hearing has been put on hold by a judge's stay.

permits.action: Data Center Customer Ratepayer Protection Act of 2026 applies to new large loads contracted after July 1, 2026
permits.summary: The act (17 O.S. 900-906) covers new data centers, crypto mining and AI computing facilities that contract for 75 MW or more per facility, or in aggregate behind one interconnection point, after July 1, 2026. For land bought outside an industrial park or municipality, the buyer must notify the OCC, county commissioners and abutting owners within 60 days, and large-load customers must file extra documentation before opening.
permits.schedule_impact: Adds land-purchase notice and pre-opening documentation steps for new large data center loads in Oklahoma.

permits.action: Advances ban on data centers in light business district
permits.summary: Columbia Borough in Lancaster County voted to advance rules prohibiting data centers in its light business district, pending county planning commission review before a final vote.
permits.schedule_impact: Narrows where data centers can go in this Lancaster County borough; no direct effect on the city campus is reported.

permits.action: Backs proposed Lockport and Cambria data center moratoriums
permits.summary: The Niagara County Planning Board supported proposed data center moratoriums in the towns of Lockport (18 months) and Cambria (nine months) while both write regulations; neither town had received a new data center request.
permits.schedule_impact: The report lists the Lake Mariner complex in Somerset among existing county data centers but does not say the moratoriums affect it; they signal a tightening local climate for new data center sites in the county.

permits.action: Weighs stricter data center ordinance: zoning, noise, studies
permits.summary: Coweta County commissioners are revising the county data center ordinance, discussing limiting data centers to industrial (M) zoning with a conditional-use permit, low-frequency noise limits and requiring noise studies before applications are filed.
permits.schedule_impact: If adopted, the revised ordinance would raise the bar for new data center sites in Coweta County; no vote date has been set.

permits.action: Title V operating permit application acknowledged
permits.summary: MDEQ acknowledged receipt of Amazon's Title V application for the Madison megasite, and no decision is recorded.
permits.schedule_impact: MDEQ's record for Amazon's Madison site lists the Title V application as acknowledged on June 29, 2026, with no decision shown.

permits.action: Takes comment on SALDO amendment for large-load projects
permits.summary: Indiana County commissioners took public comment through July 20 on a proposed amendment to the county Subdivision and Land Development Ordinance aimed at community impacts of large electric load and large-scale industrial projects; residents spoke at the same meeting about proposed data centers and a gas power plant in Center Township.
permits.schedule_impact: The county says the amendment does not approve any specific project and it has received no SALDO applications for data centers; if adopted, it could add county land-development conditions for large-load projects in the area.
permits.source: Indiana County Board of Commissioners minutes

permits.action: Commissioners table creation of the two incentive districts
permits.summary: About 200 people attended the final public hearing in McAlester on June 22, 2026, and a clear majority of those who spoke opposed the project. Commissioners voted to table creating the two tax incentive districts; the review committee will look at new cost estimates before commissioners act again.
permits.schedule_impact: The incentive districts remain uncreated until commissioners act again after the committee reviews new cost estimates.

permits.action: Developers of a Lordstown-area data center project ask Ohio Supreme Court to order site-plan review
permits.summary: Bristolville 25 Developer and BHGH Properties, which want to build a data center on 133 acres in Trumbull and Mahoning counties, filed a June 18 motion in their pending Ohio Supreme Court case asking the court to make the Village review their site plan now under the rules in place before its moratorium.
permits.schedule_impact: The ruling will show whether Lordstown's moratorium can be applied to a project whose developers say they submitted their site plan before the pause; the source does not say how this project relates to the Stargate campus.

permits.action: OG&E files large-load tariff for data centers
permits.summary: OG&E filed a draft large-load tariff with the Oklahoma Corporation Commission covering customers planning to use 75 MW or more, who would pay for estimated usage and their own grid connections and pay monthly fees to fund credits for other customers. The review could take about six months, and OG&E will announce in-person public comment.
permits.schedule_impact: OG&E says no companies are affected right away; approval could take around six months.

permits.action: 180-day data center permit moratorium extended
permits.summary: With the current 180-day data center moratorium about to expire, council approved by emergency reading another 180 days starting July 5, 2026. A village consultant has discussed zoning standards the village could adopt for data centers.
permits.schedule_impact: Keeps the village's data center moratorium in place for another 180 days while council reviews the issue and possible rules.

permits.action: Adopts one-year moratorium on new data centers in unincorporated areas
permits.summary: Boone County commissioners unanimously adopted a one-year moratorium, lasting through June 15, 2027, that halts the filing, processing and review of applications for new data centers in parts of the county outside city and town boundaries, as recommended by the Area Plan Commission.
permits.schedule_impact: The county will not file, process or review applications for new data centers in unincorporated Boone County until the moratorium ends in June 2027.

permits.agency: Office of the Governor of Texas
permits.action: Governor directs data centers to fully fund grid infrastructure
permits.summary: A June 10, 2026 gubernatorial directive says data centers must fully fund the costs of the electric infrastructure needed to serve them. The source does not say who received it.
permits.schedule_impact: Puts the cost of grid infrastructure for data centers on the data centers; the source does not describe how it applies to individual campuses.

permits.action: Enacts one-year moratorium on data centers
permits.summary: Ellsworth Township in the Mahoning Valley enacted a one-year, renewable moratorium so officials can review township zoning as it relates to potential data centers; no data center zoning applications had been received.
permits.schedule_impact: The source does not tie this to the Lordstown campus; it shows another Mahoning Valley township pausing data centers for a year while it reviews its zoning, with no applications received.

permits.action: Southaven residents file class action against xAI over turbine noise and vibration
permits.summary: Southaven residents sued xAI and its subsidiary MZX Tech in federal court, describing near-constant noise, vibration and other harms they say began in mid-2025 and hurt their quality of life and property values.
permits.schedule_impact: Comes after an earlier 2026 NAACP suit alleging the turbines run without environmental permits; no ruling is reported in the source.

permits.action: IDEM cites air-permit violations; no enforcement yet
permits.summary: IDEM's June 8 letter said Amazon installed two backup diesel generators rated 1,600 kW where the permit approved 1,500 kW units, operated emission units without first submitting an affidavit of construction, and had exhaust-temperature sensor failures in its emissions controls. IDEM said it will not take legal action now but may if violations recur.
permits.schedule_impact: No enforcement action now, but IDEM has signaled it could act if violations recur.

permits.action: Informational hearing on Emerald project plan and incentive districts
permits.summary: Pittsburg County commissioners noticed an informational hearing on June 8, 2026 and a public-comment hearing on June 22, 2026 (6 p.m., McAlester) on the Emerald ProjectCo Data Center project plan and Incentive Districts No. 1 and No. 2 (about 2,000 acres) under the Oklahoma Local Development Act, offering partial property-tax abatement.
