permits.schedule_impact: The June 22 hearing is described as the chance to be heard before any votes are taken to adopt the plan and create the districts.

permits.agency: IDEM (401 WQC 2025-78-71-ENH-WQC-2) / U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (LRE-2024-00058-171-S25)
permits.action: IDEM notices public hearing on Amazon's resubmitted wetland/stream permit request
permits.summary: IDEM's notice describes Amazon's resubmitted request for its New Carlisle campus, utility pumping station and substations, with about 4.9 acres of wetland and 3,986 feet of stream permanently impacted. A virtual hearing was scheduled for July 8, 2026 and the comment deadline was extended to July 10; mitigation includes onsite wetland creation and purchased stream credits. The notice shows no decision.
permits.schedule_impact: The notice lists both IDEM and Army Corps numbers for the request; no decision appears in it.

permits.action: Google (Jupiter Star Holdings) files reduced site plan revision
permits.summary: With Crusoe withdrawn, Google (Jupiter Star Holdings) is seeking re-approval with a smaller plan: four buildings instead of five (3,080,000 sq ft, down from 4,025,500), two permanent entrances on US 85 instead of one, and a peak construction workforce of 2,500 instead of 5,000. The county said it will handle the revision administratively because the plan is much smaller.
permits.schedule_impact: Administrative handling means the revision is not routed through a new public hearing in the county's description.
permits.source: Laramie County Board of Commissioners memo

permits.action: OPSB approves 250 MW Socrates the Younger plant plus battery
permits.summary: The Ohio Power Siting Board approved Will-Power OH's Socrates the Younger facility, a 250 MW gas plant with 116 MW of batteries on 109 acres in New Albany, to serve Meta affiliate Sidecat behind the meter, subject to 36 conditions (Case 26-0169-EL-BLN).
permits.schedule_impact: Adds approved off-grid capacity for growth at the New Albany campus.

permits.action: Microsoft request to reopen tariff case declined
permits.summary: Microsoft asked the PSC in June 2026 to reopen the tariff case over what it called errors and inconsistencies in the We Energies contract, and the commission refused.
permits.schedule_impact: Left the tariff order as decided, so Microsoft went ahead and signed the contract.

permits.agency: Wyoming regulator (not named in Black Hills release)
permits.action: Black Hills files Large Customer Transmission Cost Adjustment Mechanism
permits.summary: Black Hills filed a Large Customer Transmission Cost Adjustment Mechanism in June 2026; its Sept 30, 2026 agreements with Google run through 2048, covering up to 590 MW of grid service and a 2.1 GW third-party microgrid.
permits.schedule_impact: Decides how transmission costs for the 2.7 GW load are recovered.

permits.action: Invokes 180-day municipal cure to write data center rules
permits.summary: Nescopeck Borough Council in Luzerne County voted to declare that its zoning is silent on data centers and invoked a 180-day municipal cure period, which shields the borough from new development applications while it decides where data centers may go and sets setbacks and environmental and noise limits.
permits.schedule_impact: No developer has approached the borough, so the direct effect is limited; it adds to a pattern of nearby municipalities tightening data center rules.

permits.action: Passes data center ordinance for limited commercial district
permits.summary: Penn Township in Lancaster County passed an ordinance allowing data centers in its limited commercial district with zoning hearing board approval, with setbacks, noise limits and a closed-loop cooling requirement.
permits.schedule_impact: Shows Lancaster-area townships writing water-use and cooling conditions into data center approvals; no direct effect on the city campus is reported.

permits.action: Enacts six-month moratorium on AI data centers
permits.summary: Braceville Township enacted a six-month moratorium on AI data centers, with a trustee saying he senses a consensus among Trumbull County townships to halt data center development given concerns such as pollution and noise.
permits.schedule_impact: The source does not tie this to the Lordstown campus; it adds another Mahoning Valley township pause on AI data centers for about six months, with trustees describing broad support across Trumbull County townships.

permits.action: Approves six-month pause on data center zoning approvals
permits.summary: Howland Township trustees in Trumbull County approved a six-month moratorium, renewable for another six months, on accepting or approving zoning certificates, conditional use permits, variances or rezonings for data centers in all township zoning districts.
permits.schedule_impact: Extends the Trumbull County pattern of temporary bans, which may constrain where related data center development could go during the pause.

permits.action: Denies DeSoto Innovation District that listed data center use
permits.summary: The Olive Branch Planning Commission denied plans for the nearly 600-acre DeSoto Innovation District, whose documents had listed a data center as a conditional use, and discussed stricter guidelines for future data center applications.
permits.schedule_impact: Indicates Olive Branch planners are scrutinizing data center uses and considering stricter guidelines; the source does not link the denial to any other project.

permits.action: Approves moratorium on new data center applications and hearings
permits.summary: In June 2026 Coweta County commissioners approved a moratorium barring the county from accepting permit, land-use, rezoning, conditional-use and variance applications or holding hearings on new data centers, set to expire Dec. 23 or sooner if the board adopts ordinance amendments; five vested projects are exempt.
permits.schedule_impact: Until the pause ends or ordinance amendments pass, Coweta County will not accept or hear new data center applications, though five vested projects can proceed.

permits.action: 75 South data center applications withdrawn before hearing
permits.summary: The developer of the 292-acre 75 South Data Center Campus on Tomochichi Road in Spalding County, Georgia withdrew its four zoning applications before the Board of Commissioners' hearing, after the planning commission voted 5-0 to recommend denial of the land-use map change, and said it would resubmit.
permits.schedule_impact: The developer said it would withdraw and refile, so the proposal, which includes a separate power station, could return through the planning commission; the source gives July 27 and Aug. 25 as earliest rehearing dates and does not say whether it has refiled.

permits.action: Rejected 12-month citywide data center moratorium, 9-1
permits.summary: Cheyenne's City Council defeated on second reading, 9-1, a proposed 12-month moratorium on data center development within city limits that would have exempted operating and under-construction facilities and ordered staff to study effects on the grid, electricity rates, water use and the environment.
permits.schedule_impact: With the ordinance defeated, no citywide hold on new data center development applies within Cheyenne limits.

permits.action: Stops recruiting and incentivizing future hyperscale data centers
permits.summary: El Paso City Council voted unanimously to stop actively recruiting future hyperscale data centers and to exclude them from tax abatements, fee waivers, grants and similar incentives, without banning data centers, and the city released a draft policy framework the same day.
permits.schedule_impact: The article says the measure does not affect Meta's planned Northeast El Paso data center or its 2023 agreement; it bears on future hyperscale projects in the city.

permits.action: Recommends county data center zoning amendment to County Council
permits.summary: Luzerne County's planners sent County Council a zoning amendment for the 19 municipalities that use county zoning, including Huntington, Union and Conyngham townships; it would require Zoning Hearing Board special exception approval for every data center and setbacks of at least 2,000 feet (reducible to 1,500) for hyperscale and major centers from homes and sensitive receptors such as schools and hospitals.
permits.schedule_impact: Does not cover Salem Township itself, but would set tight siting terms for any data center growth in county-zoned townships nearby; Council still needs an introduction vote, public hearing and majority approval and may change it.

permits.action: Federal right-of-way for Green Chile gas lateral
permits.summary: After a 14-day expedited environmental review by Interior, BLM approved a right-of-way across about 16 miles of federal land for Transwestern's 24-inch gas pipeline to feed Project Jupiter, and said it is still finalizing the right-of-way authorizations.
permits.schedule_impact: Construction follows once approvals are complete; Energy Transfer filed the project with FERC under its blanket certificate process, and the article does not say whether FERC has authorized it.

permits.action: Robinson substation CPCN approved
permits.summary: Black Hills reports that the certificate for the Robinson substation, needed to serve Google's planned Cheyenne data center, was approved in May 2026. The release does not name the regulator; for a CPCN in Wyoming that is the PSC.
permits.schedule_impact: Clears a grid-connection piece for service starting late 2027.

permits.action: Passes rules allowing industrial-zone data centers by hearing
permits.summary: Ephrata Township in Lancaster County passed rules allowing data centers in its industrial zone with zoning hearing board approval.
permits.schedule_impact: Part of a countywide wave of local data center rules; no direct effect on the city campus is reported.

permits.action: Adopts 180-day pause on data center permits and applications
permits.summary: Niles City Council passed an emergency 180-day moratorium on issuing new data center permits and processing applications, after Bitdeer presented plans for 1047 Belmont Ave. and residents raised water-use, noise and infrastructure concerns, while a consultant helps draft restrictive language.
permits.schedule_impact: Signals that neighboring Trumbull County cities are restricting new data centers, which may limit nearby sites for related or follow-on development.

permits.action: Discusses possible moratorium on data center permits
permits.summary: Southington Township trustees discussed whether to consider a data center moratorium, with the zoning board to take the first step and decide what to bring to trustees; the article notes Lordstown planned to extend its own moratorium by 180 days.
permits.schedule_impact: Indicates township-level restrictions may keep spreading around the Lordstown campus.

permits.action: Extends data center moratorium; releases draft data center ordinance
permits.summary: Pittsfield Township, whose trustees approved a data center moratorium in November 2025, extended it in May 2026 and released a draft ordinance regulating data centers and other high resource demand facilities for Planning Commission review.
permits.schedule_impact: The source does not connect this township to the Saline campus; it shows one township pausing data center approvals while it writes rules, with a first Planning Commission meeting on the draft set for June 18. The extension's end date was not reported.

permits.action: Approves ordinance limiting data centers to industrial zones
permits.summary: LaPorte County commissioners unanimously approved a data center ordinance for unincorporated areas that limits them to industrial zones, requires Board of Zoning Appeals approval, sets setback and noise standards and requires fire department training, calling it a living document.
permits.schedule_impact: Sets siting and approval rules for data centers in unincorporated LaPorte County; the source does not mention the New Carlisle campus, and commissioners expect further changes.

permits.action: Discusses two-year moratorium on large-scale data centers
permits.summary: Amarillo Mayor Cole Stanley led a discussion of a temporary two-year moratorium on large-scale data centers so the city can study effects on infrastructure, water and energy, and the item was sent back to city staff, with the definition of large-scale still undecided.
permits.schedule_impact: The station notes Project Matador is not inside Amarillo city limits, so any city pause would not obviously reach the campus itself.

permits.action: PUC adopts large load customer model tariff
permits.summary: In docket M-2025-3054271, the PUC adopted a model tariff for interconnecting and serving large-load customers such as hyperscale data centers. The final order was served May 12, and the PUC ruled on reconsideration petitions on June 4 and July 16, 2026.
permits.schedule_impact: Sets the template for collateral, minimum-load and exit terms that Pennsylvania utilities will apply to new data-center service.

permits.action: Adopts six-month moratorium on data center proposals
permits.summary: Weathersfield Township trustees unanimously approved a six-month moratorium on data center proposals in the township so the zoning commission can review data center impacts and recommend zoning amendments, restrictions or prohibitions; Niles separately halted annexation talks over a Belmont Avenue data center property.
permits.schedule_impact: The source does not link this to the Lordstown campus; it shows a township pause on data center proposals, with nearby Niles also halting annexation talks and keeping its own pause on data center permits.

permits.action: Modifies and approves We Energies VLC and bespoke tariffs
permits.summary: Commissioners amended We Energies' very large customer and bespoke resource tariffs: eligibility dropped from 500 MW to 100 MW, a capacity-only option that let data centers pay 75% of generating costs was removed so they pay 100%, minimum terms became 15 years, and the utility must address the risk of shifting transmission costs to other customers.
permits.schedule_impact: Sets tougher cost terms for large data center customers of We Energies; the source does not mention Microsoft.

permits.agency: Pittsburg County Tax Incentive District Review Committee
permits.action: Review committee unanimously endorses project plan and two districts
permits.summary: On April 21, 2026 the Pittsburg County tax incentive district review committee voted to advance the Project Emerald tax plans, a roughly 2,000-acre development south of Kiowa, to the participating taxing boards and the county commission.
permits.schedule_impact: Moved the plan to the taxing boards and county commission; no final vote date was set, though public meetings were planned for May.

permits.agency: Dickey County Board of County Commissioners
permits.action: New county zoning ordinance makes data centers a conditional use
permits.summary: Dickey County's new Zoning Ordinance and Subdivision Regulations, effective April 21, 2026, define data centers (including cryptocurrency mining) and list them as a conditional use in the Agricultural District, with Planning and Zoning Commission hearings and a Board of County Commissioners decision on each permit.
permits.schedule_impact: New data center sites or expansions in the county's Agricultural District would need a conditional use permit decided by the county board.

permits.action: PSC fast-tracks Entergy request for seven more gas plants
permits.summary: On a 4-1 vote the PSC put Entergy's application for seven more gas plants for a second Meta data center in Richland Parish on an accelerated schedule of under eight months, skipping competitive bidding. A final vote is set for Nov. 18; the plants would bring the total to ten with the three already approved.
permits.schedule_impact: The Nov. 18 final PSC vote decides whether the gas plants for Meta's second Richland Parish data center go ahead.

permits.action: NAACP Clean Air Act suit over unpermitted Southaven turbines
permits.summary: In case 3:26-cv-00074, the NAACP alleges xAI and MZX Tech ran 'temporary' turbines in Southaven without the required permits, and it seeks an injunction, best-available control technology and daily penalties.
permits.schedule_impact: An injunction could shut down the interim turbines that power Colossus 2 before permanent units or grid power are available.

permits.action: SELC requests evidentiary hearing to vacate xAI PSD permit
permits.summary: For the NAACP, Safe and Sound Coalition and Young, Gifted & Green, SELC asked MDEQ to reverse, stay or vacate the PSD permit, citing emission offsets, modeling, BACT and Open Meetings Act defects.
permits.schedule_impact: A stay or remand would hold up the permanent turbine build-out in Southaven.

permits.action: Voters require referendum on future TIFs over $10M
permits.summary: Voters passed a measure giving residents a vote on TIF districts over $10 million, and business and trade groups have sued to overturn it.
permits.schedule_impact: Does not reach the TIF already approved for this campus, but would apply to any new TIF for later phases.

permits.action: AG and environmental groups appeal MPSC contract approval
permits.summary: Attorney General Nessel appealed the MPSC approval without a contested case hearing, and Earthjustice, Sierra Club, MEC and NRDC filed their own separate brief; the court consolidated the appeals and briefs were filed in August 2026.
permits.schedule_impact: A remand to a contested case could reopen the terms of the campus's power contracts.

permits.action: Gas-fired power plant air permit applications withdrawn
permits.summary: In April the developer, Yucca Growth Infrastructure, withdrew its first air quality applications for natural gas plants and proposed a fuel-cell microgrid instead. NMED has said it will hold a public hearing on the new application, with no date set.
permits.schedule_impact: Air permitting restarted on the new fuel-cell design; the source gives no decision date.

permits.action: We Energies very-large-customer rate with credit-rating collateral rule
permits.summary: In April 2026 the PSC approved a rate structure for We Energies' very large customers that requires data center operators to cover the cost of new power plants and post collateral if their credit rating falls below a set threshold. The PSC declined We Energies' June request to reconsider.
permits.schedule_impact: Oracle, whose rating S&P cut to BBB- on July 9, could owe over $100 million a year in collateral; We Energies said the project remains on track.

permits.action: Appeals court rules against Digital Gateway rezonings
permits.summary: The Court of Appeals decided the rezoning cases against the Digital Gateway approvals but stayed its decision until July 29, 2026. It upheld the separate comprehensive plan amendment.
permits.schedule_impact: The rezonings stayed in effect only until the stay ended on July 29.

permits.action: Fermi files second air permit application for 5 GW more
permits.summary: Fermi filed a second clean-air permit application with TCEQ for another 5 GW of on-site generation, which would bring the campus target to about 17 GW.
permits.schedule_impact: The filing adds 5 GW to the campus's air permit requests; the source gives no decision date.

permits.action: Groups petition to overturn Georgia Power certification
permits.summary: Environmental and faith groups represented by SELC and the Sierra Club asked the court to reverse the PSC certification order and the reconsideration denial, seeking decertification of at least 757 MW.
permits.schedule_impact: A reversal could shrink or delay capacity Georgia Power is building for new data-center load.

permits.action: EHB refuses to consolidate the two permit appeals
permits.summary: Judge Labuskes denied Homer City's motion, backed by DEP, to merge the youth appeal with the Clean Air Council appeal, finding the claims distinct.
permits.schedule_impact: The two appeals proceed on separate tracks, which could prolong permit uncertainty.

permits.action: Five state-trust-land applications for pipeline, power line rejected
permits.summary: The land commissioner turned down four rights-of-way, including one for the gas pipeline and one for a transmission line, plus a meter-station business lease across about 1.1 miles of trust land.
permits.schedule_impact: Forced the Green Chile lateral to find a route around state trust land, adding to the delay in gas supply.

permits.action: NRC notice of intent to prepare EIS; scoping opens
permits.summary: In a Federal Register notice (docket NRC-2026-0100), the NRC said it will prepare an EIS for Fermi America's four AP1000 reactors (Project Matador, Carson County, Texas), under a pilot in which the applicant prepares the draft EIS under NRC supervision. Scoping comments were due April 20, 2026.
permits.schedule_impact: The notice gives no dates for the draft or final EIS; the NRC will publish the draft for comment after reviewing the applicant's draft.

permits.action: Raises PHL100 consumptive use to 0.129 mgd
permits.summary: At its March 12, 2026 meeting SRBC approved a modification of Amazon's PHL100 data center campus approval (Docket 20240901) in Salem Township, Luzerne County, raising total consumptive use to up to 0.129 mgd on a 30-day average.
permits.schedule_impact: Raises the campus's approved consumptive water use limit to 0.129 mgd.

permits.action: Permit Board approves air permit for 41 permanent turbines
permits.summary: After a February 17 public hearing, the Permit Board voted unanimously to allow xAI subsidiary MZX Tech to build 41 permanent gas turbines at the Southaven site.
permits.schedule_impact: Approves permanent on-site turbine power for the Southaven facility.

permits.agency: St. Albans Township Board of Trustees
permits.action: Removes data processing uses from conditional uses list
permits.summary: St. Albans Township trustees adopted, by a resolution dated March 10, 2026, a zoning text amendment (application Z-25-29) removing data processing services, internet service providers, web search portals and similar uses from the conditionally permitted uses in Section 1502 of the General Business District, as the township Zoning Commission recommended.
permits.schedule_impact: Removes data processing and related uses from the conditional uses available in this Licking County township's business district; the packet does not address data center rules elsewhere in the township.

permits.action: Prohibits new data centers in every city zoning district
permits.summary: Through Ordinance 26-0-12, which updated chapters 200 and 400 of its Unified Development Ordinance, the City of Fayetteville, Georgia prohibits new data centers in every city zoning district as of March 5, 2026.
permits.schedule_impact: The city's page lists the existing QTS campus on Highway 54 West separately; the ban covers new data centers, so any future data center development in Fayetteville would face this prohibition.

permits.agency: Third Judicial District Court (Judge Jennifer DeLaney)
permits.action: Judge lets challenge to IRB ordinances proceed, orders county record
permits.summary: Two residents represented by the NM Environmental Law Center sued in October 2025 over the county's $165 billion in industrial revenue bonds and incentives. State District Judge Jennifer DeLaney did not dismiss the case, said the petitioners may be entitled to relief, and ordered the county to provide the full administrative record.
permits.schedule_impact: The petitioners argue the ordinances are void; the case continues and no further proceedings had been scheduled.

permits.action: PSC approves 600 MW Cypress Solar + storage and cost recovery
permits.summary: Entergy Arkansas applied in September 2025 for a certificate for a 600 MW solar and 350 MW battery project interconnecting at the White Bluff substation. The PSC approved the facility in March 2026, with cost recovery through the Generating Arkansas Jobs Act rider and an independent monitor to oversee costs.
permits.schedule_impact: Expected in service by the end of 2028; the filing does not link the project to Google.

permits.action: Updates data center ordinance first adopted last fall
permits.summary: Manor Township in Lancaster County updated its data center ordinance, which allows data centers on industrial parcels of 30-plus acres with zoning hearing board approval, a 40-foot height limit and nighttime noise limits.
permits.schedule_impact: Sets a hearing-based path with height and noise limits for data centers in this Lancaster-area township; no direct effect on the city campus is reported.

permits.action: TCEQ approves air permits for gas plant, denies contested-case hearing requests
permits.summary: On February 25, 2026 TCEQ commissioners approved air permits for the gas power plant serving Fermi America's data center project and voted not to grant contested-case hearings sought by groups including the Panhandle First Coalition, citing lack of standing.
permits.schedule_impact: Clears the air-permit step for the gas plant; the coalition has retained legal counsel.

permits.agency: Washtenaw County Circuit Court (Judge Julia Owdziej)
permits.action: Resident's bid to intervene in consent judgment denied
permits.summary: The judge ruled that a neighbor's motion to intervene came too late and that her Open Meetings Act claim had no merit because the board voted in public.
permits.schedule_impact: Keeps the consent judgment, and the nearly 200-worker build, in place.

permits.action: Denies reconsideration of 10 GW certification, 3-2
permits.summary: On a 3-2 vote, the PSC rejected the SELC and Sierra Club request to reconsider the December certification, including their request to deny several gas plants such as the two new McIntosh units.
permits.schedule_impact: Closed out the agency stage, so challengers turned to superior court.

permits.action: Orders data center best-practices guide and 380 agreement review
permits.summary: On a 5-3 vote, El Paso City Council told the city manager to prepare a best-practices guide for any future data center proposals and the city attorney to review current 380 agreements for data center projects.
permits.schedule_impact: Points to tighter city review of future data center proposals in El Paso; the article does not tie it to any change for existing projects.

permits.action: Council declines raw-water sale contract for data center cooling
permits.summary: McAlester councilors would not authorize the mayor to sign a contract selling raw water at $1 per 1,000 gallons for cooling at the IREN site, even though they had authorized negotiations in August 2025.
permits.schedule_impact: The project has no cooling-water contract with McAlester. IREN says the City of Kiowa has enough water for operations.

permits.agency: Doña Ana County litigation (court not named in source)
permits.action: Open Meetings Act suit over Sept 19 closed session
permits.summary: The NM Environmental Law Center filed a second suit in February 2026 alleging commissioners went into closed session shortly before the Sept 19 IRB vote without making the specific declaration the Open Meetings Act requires. The suit is still pending.
permits.schedule_impact: Pending; the source does not say what remedy is sought.

permits.action: IEDC grants 35-year data center sales tax exemption
permits.summary: At the February 2026 groundbreaking, the state disclosed a 35-year sales tax exemption for the $10 billion campus that depends on at least $1 billion invested within six years, with possible extensions up to 50 years.
permits.schedule_impact: The exemption requires at least $1 billion invested within six years, with five-year extensions up to 50 years total for further investment within 17 years; Meta hopes the first phase is online in late 2027 or early 2028.

permits.action: School board approves JETI abatement for Kilby plant
permits.summary: After the comptroller's office recommended approval in late January 2026, the Pecos-Barstow-Toyah school board approved Chevron subsidiary Energy Forge One's JETI tax-abatement application for a West Texas gas plant intended for data center use in February 2026. Microsoft says it has no definitive agreement with Chevron.
permits.schedule_impact: Grants the state-funded tax abatement sought for the plant; Microsoft's role is still under discussion.

permits.action: Places six-month moratorium on data center development
permits.summary: York Township announced a six-month, extendable moratorium due to start in March 2026, while the board seeks a formal proposal from developer Sansone Group and the planning commission works on stronger zoning language.
permits.schedule_impact: The source does not mention the Saline Township campus; it shows a separate proposed data center in York Township paused for roughly six months, with no extension confirmed.

permits.action: Residents' mandamus suit over permit hearing and rezoning notice
permits.summary: Kathryn Haushalter and other residents sued Saline Township on Jan. 28, 2026 in Washtenaw County Circuit Court, saying the ZBA failed to hold a required hearing on a permit for temporary structures and fencing at the data center site and that the clerk refused to publish notice of the township board's Jan. 14 rezoning approval.
permits.schedule_impact: Pending before Judge Julia Owdziej; no ruling reported as of the Feb. 20, 2026 article.

permits.agency: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit (transferred from Fifth Circuit)
permits.action: Susquehanna's appeal of FERC ISA orders voluntarily dismissed
permits.summary: Susquehanna Nuclear's petitions against FERC, filed in the Fifth Circuit and transferred to the Third Circuit, were dismissed on Jan 28, 2026 after the company filed an unopposed motion to dismiss on Jan 23.
permits.schedule_impact: Ends the court challenge without a ruling on the merits.

permits.action: Denies Highway 85 North data center site plan; appeal withdrawn
permits.summary: Fayetteville's Planning & Zoning Commission denied the site plan for a Crow Holdings data center north of the Fayette Pavilion on Highway 85 North on January 27, 2026, and the developer withdrew its City Council appeal on March 18, 2026.
permits.schedule_impact: Shows the city blocked a data center proposal beyond the existing QTS campus, its only data center campus; the page also reports that new data centers have been prohibited in all city zoning districts since March 5, 2026.

permits.action: Wetland, stream and floodplain permit
permits.summary: EGLE issued the permit on January 16, 2026 allowing loss of 9.12 acres of wetland, with 13.68 acres of wetland to be acquired as mitigation. It also covers temporary stream disturbance, a culvert, stormwater structures discharging to the Saline River and other waters, and outfalls in the 100-year floodplain.
permits.schedule_impact: Authorizes wetland, stream and floodplain work at the site.

permits.action: Permit to install for diesel backup generators
permits.summary: EGLE issued the air permit for 14 diesel backup generators and a fire pump about three months after granting an Oct 17, 2025 waiver that let construction begin early.
permits.schedule_impact: Closed out the site's main air permit, so backup power is not a schedule constraint.

permits.action: Hearing on data center ordinance with setbacks, noise limits
permits.summary: Henry County, Georgia commissioners held a public hearing on January 6, 2026 on a proposed ordinance that would confine data centers to M-1 and M-2 zones with a conditional use permit, require 200-foot buffers, 500-foot and 1,000-foot setbacks, 55/45 dBA noise limits and a ban on open evaporative cooling.
permits.schedule_impact: Alongside the Henry County Water Authority's rule making users above 100,000 gallons a day pay for feasibility studies, the proposal would tighten conditions for large data center users in the county; no final vote date had been set.

permits.action: Directs staff to draft data center best-practices guide
permits.summary: El Paso County's commissioners court directed staff to build a best-practices guide for data centers focused on community engagement and on assessing impacts to water and electricity, after a commissioner called for ground rules before more projects arrive.
permits.schedule_impact: The discussion was framed around the Meta campus off US 54 and Stan Roberts Sr. Avenue; the guide could shape county expectations for later data center projects, but no binding rule was adopted.

permits.action: City council votes to intervene in McCloud PUC case
permits.summary: El Paso City Council voted in mid-January 2026 to take part in El Paso Electric's application to the Public Utility Commission of Texas for the McCloud plant, and asked for more information about the project.
permits.schedule_impact: The city becomes a participant in the case; some sources say the aim is to keep residents from paying for the plant.

permits.action: QTS files DRI for 313-acre ATL2 East expansion
permits.summary: In mid-January 2026, QTS filed a Development of Regional Impact with the Georgia Department of Community Affairs for ATL2 East, a roughly 2 million sq ft data center on about 313 acres in Fayetteville; no outcome was found in the source.
permits.schedule_impact: The regional impact review is the pending step reported for the expansion.

permits.action: NPDES application for cooling-water discharge to Susquehanna
permits.summary: As of January 26, 2026, Amazon Data Services had applied to DEP for an NPDES permit to discharge used cooling water, described as continuous but intermittent, into the Susquehanna River near Salem Township, Luzerne County. The article gives no decision timeline.
permits.schedule_impact: The discharge is not authorized until DEP acts on the permit.

permits.action: County approves original Project Jade (Crusoe) campus
permits.summary: Laramie County commissioners voted unanimously in early January 2026 to approve Project Jade, the Tallgrass-Crusoe AI data center south of Cheyenne on Terry Bison Road, now planned at up to 2.7 GW. Neighbors criticized the project and asked commissioners to reconsider.
permits.schedule_impact: Gave the original Project Jade campus county approval; neighbors asked for reconsideration.

permits.action: Certifies ~10 GW of new Georgia Power resources
permits.summary: The PSC unanimously certified nearly 10,000 MW of new gas, battery and solar resources sought mainly to serve data-center load growth, and that certification is now challenged in court.
permits.schedule_impact: This is the generation backbone for new large loads on Georgia Power's system, so a court-ordered decertification would cut into planned supply.

permits.action: MPSC approves DTE 1.4 GW data center contracts without a contested case
permits.summary: Without a contested case, the MPSC approved DTE's roughly 19-year power supply and 15-year storage contracts, leaving DTE shareholders exposed to unrecovered costs and requiring a general data center tariff.
permits.schedule_impact: Approves power supply and storage contracts for the campus, with the condition that a generally applicable data center tariff be developed and reviewed in a contested case.

permits.action: Youth constitutional appeal of Homer City air permit
permits.summary: Thirteen young Pennsylvanians represented by Our Children's Trust appealed the plan approval for the Homer City project as a violation of their constitutional rights to life, health and safety, and filed an amended notice of appeal on December 28, 2025.
permits.schedule_impact: A second, separate appeal that could also send the permit back to DEP.

permits.action: Orders PJM co-location rules; BTM generation rules revised
permits.summary: FERC found PJM's tariff unjust without co-location rules, ordered three new transmission service options and changes to behind-the-meter generation rules with grandfathering, and set a paper hearing on final terms that ran through spring 2026.
permits.schedule_impact: Final PJM rules will govern how the Susquehanna-AWS arrangement is classified and charged during the transition.

permits.action: Clean Air Council, PennFuture, Sierra Club appeal air permit
permits.summary: The three groups appealed the plan approval to the EHB, claiming violations of the Clean Air Act, the state Air Pollution Control Act, the Environmental Rights Amendment and DEP's environmental justice policy.
permits.schedule_impact: An EHB ruling against the permit could require DEP to redo the permit and delay construction of the plant.

permits.action: Air construction permit modification 1720-00098 issued
permits.summary: MDEQ's records show a final air construction permit modification (1720-00098) issued December 16, 2025 for the Amazon Madison Mega Site at 1978 Highway 22, Canton.
permits.schedule_impact: A final modified air construction permit is on file for the site.

permits.action: Major (PSD) air permit for VoltaGrid power plant
permits.summary: VoltaGrid LLC applied to TCEQ on Dec 12, 2025 for air permit 182467 plus PSD permits PSDTX1692 and GHGPSDTX266 for an electric power generation facility at 299 FM 604, Shackelford County; TCEQ issued notice on Dec 17, 2025.
permits.schedule_impact: TCEQ found the application administratively complete and is reviewing it on an expedited basis. Contested case hearing requests are possible for permits 182467 and PSDTX1692 but not for GHGPSDTX266.

permits.action: El Paso Electric applies to build 366 MW McCloud plant
permits.summary: El Paso Electric applied to the PUC in December for a $499 million, 366 MW natural gas plant made of 813 modular generators to power Meta's planned 1 GW El Paso data center.
permits.schedule_impact: The plant needs PUC approval; an administrative law judge proposal has recommended conditions, and no commission vote had been set.

permits.action: Invenergy Red Oak Ridge gas plant application under review
permits.summary: Red Oak Ridge Energy Center LLC, an Invenergy subsidiary, applied in December 2025 for a certificate for a gas plant of up to 1,186 MW in the Town of Paris, Kenosha County. The PSC issued a draft environmental impact statement in April 2026. No decision date is listed.
permits.schedule_impact: Construction is expected to begin in October 2026 only if approved, with operation estimated for June 30, 2030.
permits.source: Public Service Commission of Wisconsin; Civic Media

permits.action: FLUM amendment and rezoning to business park for QTS expansion
permits.summary: The council approved a future land use map amendment and rezoning to business park for two parcels that had been designated an innovation mixed-use activity center and zoned planned community district, growing the QTS east campus area from about 615 to 900 acres; the plan includes four new buildings of about two million sq ft.
permits.schedule_impact: No building permit will be issued until the state DRI review is finished and the council approves a revised development agreement.

permits.action: PSC approves Entergy Arkansas–Google power contract
permits.summary: In December, the Arkansas PSC approved an Entergy contract to supply power to Google's planned $4 billion West Memphis data center.
permits.schedule_impact: Approves the power supply contract for the planned West Memphis data center.

permits.action: Passes ordinance limiting where data centers can be built
permits.summary: Nescopeck Township supervisors in Luzerne County passed an ordinance restricting where in the township data centers may locate, and an attorney for a data center warned them of a legal fight.
permits.schedule_impact: The report does not tie it to the AWS campus; it shows siting limits, and a threat of litigation, in a township in the campus's area.

permits.action: DEP issues air plan approval 32-00457A for Homer City Redevelopment
permits.summary: DEP issued air plan approval 32-00457A on November 18, 2025 for the Homer City Redevelopment gas plant. Clean Air Council, PennFuture and Sierra Club jointly appealed it to the Environmental Hearing Board, with a press release dated December 17, 2025.
permits.schedule_impact: The air approval is under appeal at the Environmental Hearing Board.

permits.action: Ohio EPA water quality certification documents submitted for plant expansion
permits.summary: SoftBank-affiliated Crescent Dune LLC submitted water quality certification documents to Ohio EPA on Nov. 17, with a wetland and stream delineation report covering about 160 acres behind the Lordstown plant, for an expansion described as making modular data centers and server racks.
permits.schedule_impact: The article does not say whether Ohio EPA has approved, denied or is still reviewing the application.

permits.action: County forms review committee for IREN incentive districts
permits.summary: Pittsburg County commissioners voted to form the county review committee that vets the incentive-district plan for IREN's site south of Kiowa. The committee first met on December 8, 2025.
permits.schedule_impact: Started the statutory review that has to finish before the county can create the incentive districts.

permits.action: Village council passes ban on data center proposals
permits.summary: The Lordstown Village Council voted on Nov 3, 2025 for an ordinance banning all data center proposals in the village; a developer's attorney argued the council skipped a required 30-day notice. By 2026 the village was operating under a temporary 180-day moratorium instead (see the June 2026 extension).
permits.schedule_impact: Superseded by the village's temporary moratorium, which is the rule now in force.

permits.action: $458 million TIF for the data center campus
permits.summary: The city approved a $458 million tax increment financing package for the data center in November 2025.
permits.schedule_impact: Provides TIF support for the campus, which was already under construction when the article was published.

permits.action: Final plat for first three industrial lots approved 4-0
permits.summary: The Stillwater Planning Commission voted 4-0 to approve the final plat for three industrial lots (202 acres), the first phase of an eight-lot site for Google's data center, as reported Nov. 18, 2025. Building permits for Lots 1 and 2 were already approved, and the City Council must still accept the plat before it is recorded; that acceptance is not confirmed.
permits.schedule_impact: The remaining five lots will be platted later.

permits.agency: NM Office of the State Engineer
permits.action: Emergency authorization of construction-water well
permits.summary: On October 23, 2025 the State Engineer issued an emergency authorization letting Santa Teresa Capital use a new well to supply water for building Project Jupiter.
permits.schedule_impact: On August 23, 2026 the New Mexico Supreme Court stayed the authorization until further order, in a case brought by the Center for Biological Diversity.
permits.source: NM Supreme Court order, S-1-SC-41580 (via Center for Biological Diversity)

permits.action: Energy Forge One files NSR/PSD air permits for Kilby plant
permits.summary: Energy Forge One LLC applied to TCEQ on Oct 17, 2025 for air permit 181895 and PSD permits PSDTX1684 and GHGPSDTX260 for an electric power generation facility in Pecos, Reeves County; TCEQ issued its notice on Oct 24, 2025.
permits.schedule_impact: The notice lists no public meeting date; a meeting is held if the executive director finds significant interest or one is requested.

permits.agency: Washtenaw County Circuit Court / Saline Township Board
permits.action: Consent judgment allows data center after rezoning denial
permits.summary: The township board denied rezoning 4-1 on Sept 10 and Related Digital sued two days later. A consent judgment filed Oct 15 in Washtenaw County Circuit Court includes about $14 million in payments, a 55 dB noise limit, and no water use for cooling.
permits.schedule_impact: Settles the lawsuit and lets the project proceed; Related Digital planned to begin work in fall 2025.

permits.action: Council approves Fermi water supply agreement
permits.summary: Amarillo's council approved on first reading a water supply agreement letting Fermi America buy up to 2.5 million gallons a day at double the standard rate, with second reading set for Oct 28, 2025; Fermi's later SEC filings list the City of Amarillo supply as in place.
permits.schedule_impact: Gives the campus a municipal water supply for its first phases.

permits.action: Google applies for major-source air permit for backup generators
permits.summary: Google applied on September 25 to Arkansas DEQ for a Clean Air Act major emissions permit covering backup generators, which Google says would run only if the grid goes down. The article does not say whether a draft or final permit exists.
permits.schedule_impact: Generator operation depends on DEQ's action on this permit.

permits.agency: Doña Ana County Board of County Commissioners
permits.action: Up to $165B industrial revenue bonds and LEDA support
permits.summary: Commissioners passed ordinances authorizing up to $165 billion in taxable IRBs and related incentives for Project Jupiter, and residents quickly sued to void them.
permits.schedule_impact: The tax structure stays in place but could be voided if the court challenges succeed.

permits.action: Final site plan for plant expansion and data center showroom
permits.summary: The commission voted 4-0 (mayor abstaining for a stated conflict of interest) to approve three building additions and a new 145,337 sq ft proof-of-concept modular data center showroom, about 1.24 million sq ft in total, on I-1 land. A Foxconn representative said the showroom building would not be used as a working data center, only for engineering and customer demonstrations.
permits.schedule_impact: Cleared local construction of the expansion, tentatively scheduled for September 2025 through at least February 2027.

permits.action: NRC accepts Parts 1–2 of four-unit AP1000 COL application
permits.summary: The NRC finished its acceptance review and docketed Parts 1 and 2 of Fermi's combined license application for four AP1000 units. Dates for the safety evaluations, the mandatory hearing and the licensing decision are still listed as TBD.
permits.schedule_impact: NRC lists safety evaluations, the mandatory hearing and the licensing decision as TBD; its environmental review targets a draft EIS in September 2026 and a final EIS in December 2026.

permits.action: OPSB approves 200 MW Socrates North gas plant
permits.summary: The board approved Will-Power OH's 200 MW gas plant on about 20 acres in the New Albany International Business Park (Case 25-188-EL-BGN), to serve Meta affiliate Sidecat behind the meter, with 30 conditions.
permits.schedule_impact: Authorizes construction of an on-site gas plant to supply an adjacent data center without a grid connection.

permits.action: Data center moratorium in unincorporated areas, extended three times
permits.summary: Clayton County, Georgia has a moratorium pausing new data center applications and construction in unincorporated areas, extended three times since September 2025, while the City of Lovejoy is not covered and is reviewing a roughly 400-acre data center campus.
permits.schedule_impact: New data center applications in unincorporated Clayton County remain paused, though incorporated Lovejoy is outside the pause and can still review projects.

permits.action: LPSC approves Entergy settlement for three Meta gas plants
permits.summary: Commissioners voted 4-1 for a settlement letting Entergy Louisiana build three gas generating facilities and new transmission to serve Meta's data center, with Meta's contract said to cover the generation costs it causes.
permits.schedule_impact: Allows Entergy to proceed with three gas units and new transmission lines for Meta.

permits.action: Wetland fill application withdrawn after unauthorized impact
permits.summary: Because a contractor had filled nearly an acre of wetland without authorization, IDEM issued a noncompliance and stop-work notice for state waters in July 2025, and Amazon withdrew its roughly 10-acre wetland application the following month.
permits.schedule_impact: IDEM ordered work stopped in state-regulated waters; a revised application must include 30% additional mitigation for the impacted wetland, and work continued elsewhere on the site.

permits.action: Applied Digital withdraws backup-generator siting variance request
permits.summary: On August 1, 2025 Applied Digital filed a variance withdrawal request in North Dakota PSC docket PU-24-359.
permits.schedule_impact: Ends the variance request in that docket.

permits.action: PUCO adopts AEP Ohio data center tariff
permits.summary: PUCO adopted AEP Ohio's tariff for data centers over 25 MW, which requires them to pay for at least 85% of subscribed capacity for up to 12 years and sets out a phased end to AEP's moratorium on new data center service.
permits.schedule_impact: Sets terms and timing for new data center service from AEP Ohio in central Ohio; existing facilities are grandfathered unless they expand capacity beyond 25 MW.

permits.action: Reinvestment zone and Vantage tax abatement application approved
permits.summary: At a special meeting the court unanimously created Reinvestment Zone 2025-1, accepted Vantage's abatement application, and agreed to sign a 10-year deal with about $10 million a year in payments once the land closed.
permits.schedule_impact: The county stated its intent to sign a formal agreement once Vantage buys the land; if the purchase does not close within 30 days, the county would need to restart the process.

permits.action: Health department permits 15 permanent xAI turbines
permits.summary: In early July 2025 the Shelby County Health Department approved xAI's permit for 15 permanently installed turbines, with 12-month rolling emission caps that xAI must record monthly. SELC and the NAACP appealed the approval.
permits.schedule_impact: Authorizes the permanent turbines, but the approval is being challenged on appeal.

permits.action: SB 6 on interconnection and cost of service for certain electrical loads signed
permits.summary: Texas enacted SB 6, signed June 20, 2025 and effective immediately. Its title covers planning for, interconnection and operation of, and costs of serving certain electrical loads.
permits.schedule_impact: Sets the legal framework for how certain electrical loads are connected and charged in Texas; the bill's subjects include the PUC and ERCOT.

permits.action: OPSB certifies 200 MW Socrates South behind-the-meter gas plant
permits.summary: The siting board approved Williams-backed Socrates South, a 200 MW gas plant serving Meta's New Albany data center without connecting to the grid.
permits.schedule_impact: Allowed construction of the 200 MW plant, which the article says is due for completion in Q3 2026.

permits.action: Approves We Energies Oak Creek and Paris gas plants
permits.summary: On May 22, 2025 the PSC approved We Energies' proposal for two gas plants, at Oak Creek and in the Town of Paris, adding about 1,200 MW for southeast Wisconsin, largely driven by Microsoft's Mount Pleasant data center.
permits.schedule_impact: Approves new utility generation meant to meet demand largely driven by the Microsoft campus.

permits.action: County back-bills QTS for unmetered construction water
permits.summary: After low-pressure complaints in May 2025, Fayette County found QTS water lines it said had been installed without its staff's knowledge. The county later walked that claim back, blaming a smart-meter upgrade that left some QTS meters off the billing system, and billed QTS $147,000.
permits.schedule_impact: QTS says its water use is temporary and tied to construction; a closed-loop cooling system is not expected until construction ends in 2030.
permits.source: Atlanta News First; Fayette County statement

permits.action: Part 70 operating permit issued for Amazon New Carlisle source
permits.summary: IDEM issued a Part 70 operating permit for Amazon Data Services' generators at 31100 State Road 2 in New Carlisle.
permits.schedule_impact: Authorized backup-generator operation for the campus, and it is the base permit for the pending modification.

permits.action: Council approves Groot LLC agreements incl. $10B PILOT
permits.summary: In May 2025 the council approved several agreements with Groot LLC, reported to be a Google-linked entity, including a $10 billion payment-in-lieu-of-taxes arrangement for a campus on about 1,178 acres.
permits.schedule_impact: Sets local tax treatment for the proposed campus.

permits.action: Passes 180-day pause on new data center proposals
permits.summary: In May 2025 the Coweta County Commission unanimously passed a 180-day moratorium on new data center proposals, set to expire Nov. 3, 2025, while staff drafted a county ordinance with minimum standards for data centers.
permits.schedule_impact: Marked the start of Coweta County's move toward county-wide data center standards that would become zoning conditions.

permits.action: Rehearing order upholds ISA rejection
permits.summary: On rehearing, FERC affirmed its rejection, finding PJM had not shown the non-conforming agreement was both unique and necessary.
permits.schedule_impact: Ended the agency route for the original co-location deal.
permits.source: FERC brief, Susquehanna Nuclear v. FERC

permits.action: HB 1539 exempts on-site backup generation from PSC siting
permits.summary: Gov. Armstrong signed a law, effective August 1, 2025, that removes off-grid on-site backup generation over 50 MW from the PSC Siting Act and leaves approval to local authorities. Applied Digital testified in support.
permits.schedule_impact: Removes PSC siting review for large off-grid on-site backup generation, leaving approval to local authorities; environmental protections still apply.
permits.source: Office of the Governor of North Dakota

permits.action: Approves I&M large-load tariff settlement
permits.summary: The IURC approved I&M's settlement, signed by Amazon among others, that sets interconnection and tariff terms for loads of at least 70 MW, and added a rule that cuts of more than 20% in contracted capacity need commission approval.
permits.schedule_impact: Sets the service terms for the New Carlisle campus load and leaves cost allocation to later rate cases.

permits.action: PSC grants MDU certificate to serve Applied Digital expansion
permits.summary: In case PU-24-330, the PSC issued Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity No. 6006 to Montana-Dakota Utilities to serve Applied Digital in Dickey County. No objections were received.
permits.schedule_impact: Cleared retail electric service for the expanded campus.

permits.action: Adopts large-load (>100 MW) billing rule for Georgia Power
permits.summary: In a unanimous vote, the PSC let Georgia Power bill new customers above 100 MW on special terms, including upstream cost recovery, contracts of up to 15 years and minimum bills, and required those contracts to be filed with the commission for review.
permits.schedule_impact: New Georgia Power data-center service contracts now go through PSC review and carry minimum-bill terms.

permits.agency: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Memphis District
permits.action: Groot submits site plans for Corps water-mitigation approval
permits.summary: Groot, developing a $1 billion, 900,000 sq ft data center at the south end of Bollinger Road in West Memphis, submitted plans in December 2024 to the Corps' Memphis office for water-mitigation approval.
permits.schedule_impact: Corps approval of the water mitigation is part of the permitting; the article reports no decision.

permits.action: Voters approve OG&E franchise to serve data center
permits.summary: About 72% of Stillwater voters (10,250 of 14,180) approved a measure letting OG&E, rather than the city electric utility, serve Kipper LLC's data center campus, with a city franchise fee of about $2.25 million per data center per year once operating.
permits.schedule_impact: Settled OG&E as the power provider for the campus.

permits.action: Council approves TIF district, abatements and water service for Meta
permits.summary: Lebanon's council unanimously approved a new TIF district and property tax abatements for Meta's roughly 1,400-acre LEAP site, along with a plan to meet Meta's request for 3 MGD of water and 1.5 MGD of wastewater service.
permits.schedule_impact: Unblocked the land purchase and phased construction in the LEAP district.

permits.action: Rejects amended Susquehanna ISA for co-located load
permits.summary: FERC rejected PJM's amended interconnection service agreement that would have expanded behind-the-meter supply from Susquehanna to the AWS campus.
permits.schedule_impact: Capped behind-the-meter supply and pushed Talen and AWS toward a front-of-meter design.
permits.source: FERC brief, Susquehanna Nuclear v. FERC

permits.action: Approves 60,000 gpd consumptive use, first three buildings
permits.summary: SRBC approved consumptive use of 60,000 gallons per day for the first three buildings and required Amazon to return before expanding.
permits.schedule_impact: Covered water for phase one only, so later buildings needed a modification.

permits.agency: Citizens Energy Group Board of Directors
permits.action: Citizens board authorizes up to $700M SRF bonds for LEAP water
permits.summary: Citizens' board approved a resolution allowing up to $700 million in state revolving fund borrowing for the Citizens–Lebanon water supply program, which is planned to deliver up to 25 MGD to Lebanon Utilities by 2031.
permits.schedule_impact: Funds the wholesale water supply program for Lebanon Utilities, which serves customers including those in the LEAP district; Citizens will not deliver water directly to LEAP.

permits.action: Planning Commission unanimously backs data center campus plan
permits.summary: After city staff presented the campus plan on July 16, 2024, the Planning Commission voted unanimously in favor. The project, planned over up to six phases, seeks a tax incentive district of up to 25 years with payments in lieu of taxes for each phase. The land is already zoned General Industrial.
permits.schedule_impact: The taxing jurisdictions must still agree to form the incentive district.

permits.action: Approves AWS megasite site plan
permits.summary: After the Planning and Zoning Board's Feb. 8 approval, supervisors unanimously approved the AWS site plan, with five buildings in the first phase and seven more possible later.
permits.schedule_impact: Cleared the supervisors' site-plan approval for the AWS Madison County Megasite; no schedule has been set for the seven later buildings.

permits.action: Amazon incentive law; Entergy plants exempt from PSC preapproval
permits.summary: Lawmakers passed the AWS incentive package in special session, including a $215 million infrastructure loan, tax exemptions and rebates, and authority for Entergy to build power plants for the project without PSC certification; the PSC still regulates the rates Entergy charges for the project.
permits.schedule_impact: Entergy can build serving generation without PSC certification, though the PSC still regulates its rates for the project.

permits.action: City incentive agreement with Meta affiliate Wurldwide LLC
permits.summary: The city signed an incentive agreement with Meta affiliate Wurldwide LLC for a data center on about 1,000 acres in Northeast El Paso, and El Paso County offered a property tax abatement.
permits.schedule_impact: Baseline local incentives behind the campus; the Sembrando Esperanza Coalition is urging the city, county and utilities to end their contracts with Meta.
